98	class DenseIndex:
99	    """Country-segmented exact top-k cosine index over an fp16 memmap cache."""
100	
101	    def __init__(self, cache_dir: str, encoder: str, device: str, encode_batch: int):
102	        self.cache_dir = cache_dir
103	        self.encoder = encoder
104	        self.encode_batch = encode_batch
105	        self.device = _resolve_device(device)
106	        self.device_is_cuda = self.device.startswith("cuda")
107	        self.dim: int = 0
108	        self.count: int = 0
109	        self.segments: dict[str, tuple[int, int]] = {}  # country -> (start, count)
110	        self.order: np.ndarray | None = None            # memmap position -> candidate row
111	        self._memmap = None
112	        self._model = None
113	        self._segment_cache: dict[str, "torch.Tensor"] = {}
114	
115	    # -- construction -----------------------------------------------------
116	
117	    @classmethod
118	    def build(
119	        cls,
120	        candidates: pd.DataFrame,
121	        texts_by_country: dict[int, list[str]],
122	        country_ids: np.ndarray,
123	        country_names: dict[int, str],
124	        cache_dir: str,
125	        encoder: str,
126	        device: str,
127	        encode_batch: int,
128	    ) -> "DenseIndex":
129	        """Encode texts (already grouped by country) into a fresh cache."""
130	        os.makedirs(cache_dir, exist_ok=True)
131	        index = cls(cache_dir, encoder, device, encode_batch)
132	        index._load_model()
133	
134	        n = len(candidates)
135	        order = np.argsort(country_ids, kind="stable")
136	        segments: dict[str, tuple[int, int]] = {}
137	        position = 0
138	        for cid in range(len(country_names)):
139	            count = len(texts_by_country[cid])
140	            if count:
141	                segments[country_names[cid]] = (position, count)
142	                position += count
143	
144	        print(f"[dense] Encoding {n:,} candidate texts on device '{index.device}' "
145	              f"(model={encoder}, dim={index.dim}) ...")
146	        memmap_path = os.path.join(cache_dir, "embeddings.fp16.npy")
147	        memmap = np.lib.format.open_memmap(memmap_path, mode="w+", dtype=np.float16, shape=(n, index.dim))
148	        for cid in range(len(country_names)):
149	            country = country_names[cid]
150	            start, count = segments.get(country, (0, 0))
151	            texts = texts_by_country[cid]
152	            for chunk_start in range(0, count, ENCODE_CHUNK):
153	                chunk = texts[chunk_start:chunk_start + ENCODE_CHUNK]
154	                vectors = index._encode_texts(chunk)
155	                memmap[start + chunk_start:start + chunk_start + len(chunk)] = vectors.astype(np.float16)
156	                done = min(chunk_start + len(chunk), count)
157	                print(f"[dense]   {country or '<empty>'}: encoded {done:,}/{count:,}")
158	            texts_by_country[cid] = None  # free the text list as we go
159	        memmap.flush()
160	        del memmap
161	
162	        order_path = os.path.join(cache_dir, "order.npy")
163	        np.save(order_path, order.astype(np.int64))
164	        meta = {
165	            "encoder": encoder,
166	            "text_version": ENCODER_TEXT_VERSION,
167	            "dim": index.dim,
168	            "count": n,
169	            "segments": {country: [int(s), int(c)] for country, (s, c) in segments.items()},
170	        }
171	        with open(os.path.join(cache_dir, "dense_meta.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
172	            json.dump(meta, handle, indent=2)
173	        index.order = order.astype(np.int64)
174	        index.segments = segments
175	        index.count = n
176	        print(f"[dense] Cache written to {cache_dir}")
177	        return index
178	
179	    @classmethod
180	    def load(cls, cache_dir: str, encoder: str, device: str, encode_batch: int) -> "DenseIndex | None":
181	        meta_path = os.path.join(cache_dir, "dense_meta.json")
182	        order_path = os.path.join(cache_dir, "order.npy")
183	        memmap_path = os.path.join(cache_dir, "embeddings.fp16.npy")
184	        if not (os.path.isfile(meta_path) and os.path.isfile(order_path) and os.path.isfile(memmap_path)):
185	            return None
186	        with open(meta_path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
187	            meta = json.load(handle)
188	        index = cls(cache_dir, meta["encoder"], device, encode_batch)
189	        index.dim = int(meta["dim"])
190	        index.count = int(meta["count"])
191	        index.segments = {country: (int(start), int(count)) for country, (start, count) in meta["segments"].items()}
192	        index.order = np.load(order_path)
193	        index._load_model()
194	        print(f"[dense] Reusing cached embeddings: {index.count:,} vectors, "
195	              f"{len(index.segments)} countries, dim={index.dim}")
196	        return index
197	
198	    def _load_model(self):
199	        if not HAVE_DENSE:
200	            raise RuntimeError("sentence-transformers/torch not installed; dense retrieval unavailable")
201	        print(f"[dense] Loading encoder '{self.encoder}' on device '{self.device}' ...")
202	        self._model = SentenceTransformer(self.encoder, device=self.device)
203	        if self.device_is_cuda:
204	            try:
205	                self._model.half()
206	            except Exception:
207	                pass
208	        self.dim = int(self._model.get_sentence_embedding_dimension())
209	
210	    # -- search -----------------------------------------------------------
211	
212	    def _encode_texts(self, texts: list[str]) -> np.ndarray:
213	        vectors = self._model.encode(
214	            texts,
215	            batch_size=self.encode_batch,
216	            show_progress_bar=False,
217	            normalize_embeddings=True,
218	            convert_to_numpy=True,
219	        )
220	        return np.asarray(vectors, dtype=np.float32)
221	
222	    def _encode_queries(self, texts: list[str], like: "torch.Tensor") -> "torch.Tensor":
223	        vectors = self._encode_texts(texts)
224	        return torch.from_numpy(vectors).to(device=like.device, dtype=like.dtype)
225	
226	    def _segment_tensor(self, country: str):
227	        """The country's embedding block on the compute device; None if absent."""
228	        segment = self.segments.get(country)
229	        if segment is None:
230	            return None
231	        if country in self._segment_cache:
232	            return self._segment_cache[country]
233	        start, count = segment
234	        self._segment_cache.clear()  # keep at most one country resident
235	        source = np.load(os.path.join(self.cache_dir, "embeddings.fp16.npy"), mmap_mode="r")
236	        try:
237	            if self.device_is_cuda:
238	                try:
239	                    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
240	                    tensor = torch.empty((count, self.dim), dtype=torch.float16, device=self.device)
241	                    for offset in range(0, count, SEGMENT_LOAD_CHUNK):
242	                        block = np.array(source[start + offset:start + min(offset + SEGMENT_LOAD_CHUNK, count)])
243	                        tensor[offset:offset + len(block)] = torch.from_numpy(block).to(self.device)
244	                except RuntimeError as exc:
245	                    print(f"[dense] WARNING: GPU segment load failed ({exc}); "
246	                          f"falling back to CPU search for country={country!r}")
247	                    tensor = self._load_segment_cpu(start, count)
248	            else:
249	                tensor = self._load_segment_cpu(start, count)
250	        finally:
251	            del source
252	        print(f"[dense] Loaded segment {country!r}: {count:,} vectors onto {tensor.device}")
253	        self._segment_cache[country] = tensor
254	        return tensor
255	
256	    def _load_segment_cpu(self, start: int, count: int) -> "torch.Tensor":
257	        source = np.load(os.path.join(self.cache_dir, "embeddings.fp16.npy"), mmap_mode="r")
258	        try:
259	            tensor = torch.empty((count, self.dim), dtype=torch.float32)
260	            for offset in range(0, count, SEGMENT_LOAD_CHUNK):
261	                block = np.array(source[start + offset:start + min(offset + SEGMENT_LOAD_CHUNK, count)])
262	                tensor[offset:offset + len(block)] = torch.from_numpy(block).float()
263	            return tensor
264	        finally:
265	            del source
266	
267	    def search(self, s1_batch: pd.DataFrame, top_k: int) -> dict[str, list[tuple[int, float, int]]]:
268	        """Dense top-k per S1 entity: entity_id -> [(candidate row, cosine, rank)]."""
269	        if self._model is None:
270	            return {}
271	        groups: dict[str, list[tuple[str, str]]] = defaultdict(list)
272	        for entity_id, name, address, country in s1_batch[
273	            ["entity_id", "business_name", "business_address", "country"]
274	        ].itertuples(index=False, name=None):
275	            prepared = prepare_record(name, address, country)
276	            groups[str(prepared["country"])].append((entity_id, encoder_text(prepared)))
277	
278	        results: dict[str, list[tuple[int, float, int]]] = {}
279	        for country, items in groups.items():
280	            segment_tensor = self._segment_tensor(country)
281	            if segment_tensor is None or segment_tensor.shape[0] == 0:
282	                continue
283	            start, _count = self.segments[country]
284	            k = min(top_k, int(segment_tensor.shape[0]))
285	            if k <= 0:
286	                continue
287	            for group_start in range(0, len(items), QUERY_GROUP):
288	                group = items[group_start:group_start + QUERY_GROUP]
289	                queries = self._encode_queries([text for _, text in group], like=segment_tensor)
290	                best_scores = None
291	                best_positions = None
292	                for chunk_start in range(0, int(segment_tensor.shape[0]), SEARCH_CHUNK):
293	                    chunk = segment_tensor[chunk_start:chunk_start + SEARCH_CHUNK]
294	                    sims = queries @ chunk.t()
295	                    chunk_k = min(k, int(chunk.shape[0]))
296	                    scores_chunk, positions_chunk = torch.topk(sims, chunk_k, dim=1)
297	                    positions_chunk = positions_chunk + chunk_start
298	                    if best_scores is None:
299	                        best_scores, best_positions = scores_chunk, positions_chunk
300	                    else:
301	                        best_scores = torch.cat([best_scores, scores_chunk], dim=1)
302	                        best_positions = torch.cat([best_positions, positions_chunk], dim=1)
303	                        best_scores, merge_order = torch.topk(best_scores, k, dim=1)
304	                        best_positions = torch.gather(best_positions, 1, merge_order)
305	                scores_np = best_scores.float().cpu().numpy()
306	                positions_np = best_positions.cpu().numpy()
307	                for row_index, (entity_id, _text) in enumerate(group):
308	                    hits = []
309	                    for rank in range(k):
310	                        position = int(positions_np[row_index, rank])
311	                        candidate_row = int(self.order[start + position])
312	                        hits.append((candidate_row, float(scores_np[row_index, rank]), rank + 1))
313	                    results[entity_id] = hits
314	        return results
315	
316	
317	def merge_hits(
318	    lexical_hits: list[CandidateHit],
319	    dense_hits: list[tuple[int, float, int]],
320	    top_k: int,
321	) -> list[CandidateHit]:
322	    """Reciprocal-rank fusion of the two retrieval modes."""
323	    lexical_by_row = {hit.row: hit for hit in lexical_hits}
324	    dense_by_row = {row: (score, rank) for row, score, rank in dense_hits}
325	    fused: list[tuple[float, int, CandidateHit | None, float, int]] = []
326	    for row in set(lexical_by_row) | set(dense_by_row):
327	        lexical = lexical_by_row.get(row)
328	        dense_score, dense_rank = dense_by_row.get(row, (0.0, 0))
329	        score = 0.0
330	        if lexical is not None and lexical.lexical_rank:
331	            score += 1.0 / (RRF_K + lexical.lexical_rank)
332	        if dense_rank:
333	            score += 1.0 / (RRF_K + dense_rank)
334	        fused.append((score, row, lexical, dense_score, dense_rank))
335	    fused.sort(key=lambda item: (-item[0], item[1]))
336	    return [
337	        CandidateHit(
338	            row=row,
339	            retrieval_score=float(score),
340	            lexical_score=(lexical.lexical_score if lexical is not None else 0.0),
341	            lexical_pass_count=(lexical.lexical_pass_count if lexical is not None else 0),
342	            lexical_rank=(lexical.lexical_rank if lexical is not None else 0),
343	            dense_score=float(dense_score),
344	            dense_rank=int(dense_rank),
345	        )
346	        for score, row, lexical, dense_score, dense_rank in fused[:top_k]
347	    ]

441	    def retrieve_batch(self, s1_batch: pd.DataFrame, top_k: int | None = None) -> dict[str, list[CandidateHit]]:

458	def iter_country_batches(s1: pd.DataFrame, batch_size: int = 1_000):
459	    """Yield S1 batches whose rows share one country (raw column value order).
460	
461	    The dense index keeps one country segment on the device at a time, so
462	    country-grouped iteration avoids reloading a segment for every batch.
463	    """
464	    if len(s1) == 0:
465	        return
466	    country_values = s1["country"].astype(str).to_numpy()
467	    order = np.argsort(country_values, kind="stable")
468	    sorted_s1 = s1.iloc[order]
469	    for start in range(0, len(sorted_s1), batch_size):
470	        yield sorted_s1.iloc[start:start + batch_size]

502

#### Thinking

The module looks good overall. A few remaining issues I can spot:

1. **`texts_by_country: dict[int, list[str]] = defaultdict(list) if need_dense else {}`** — if not need_dense, it's a plain dict — then `texts_by_country[cid].append(...)` would fail, but that code path is guarded by `if need_dense`. OK.

2. **`DenseIndex.build` — `memmap[start + chunk_start:...] = vectors.astype(np.float16)`** — `vectors` is fp32 (or fp16 if model.half()... `_encode_texts` does `np.asarray(vectors, dtype=np.float32)` — upcast to fp32 then down to fp16 for storage. Slight double-cast but correct and simple.

3. **Model.half() + normalize_embeddings**: ST's Normalize uses torch.nn.functional.normalize — works with fp16. Encoding output fp16 → upcast fp32 in _encode_texts. Fine.

4. **`_segment_tensor` GPU OOM fallback** — catches RuntimeError from allocation; if the OOM happens during `torch.empty`, `tensor` may be undefined... Actually if `torch.empty` raises, the except catches it, calls `_load_segment_cpu`. `tensor` gets reassigned. Fine. But if OOM happens INSIDE the loop during `.to(device)` — same except catches, tensor discarded, CPU fallback. OK. Edge: partial tensor left on GPU — `tensor` name rebinds to CPU tensor; the partial GPU tensor gets garbage collected by torch's allocator eventually. Acceptable.

5. **`search()` — `best_scores is None` after first chunk if segment_tensor.shape[0] > 0** — chunks always ≥ 1, so best_scores set. OK.

6. `torch.cat` then topk: after merging, best has exactly k columns — wait, first chunk gives chunk_k = min(k, chunk) columns; subsequent cat gives chunk_k + k columns → topk(k) → k columns. Final best_scores has k columns (assuming k ≤ total... k = min(top_k, segment rows)). Correct.

Hmm wait — one subtle issue: after the first chunk, `best_positions` has chunk_k columns where chunk_k might be < k if chunk < k... SEARCH_CHUNK=250k, k ≤ 40, so chunk_k = k always in practice. Fine.

7. **`iter_country_batches` — `np.argsort` on object array**: `s1["country"].astype(str).to_numpy()` — if country column has missing values (NaN)... loaded with keep_default_na=False so empty strings, fine. Object-dtype argsort works (uses Python string comparison). For 1.73M rows, a few seconds. OK.

8. **predict/train iter order and `retrieve_batch` return keyed by `s1_batch["entity_id"]`** — for duplicate entity_ids in S1? Each S1 entity unique. OK.

9. **`DenseIndex.load` sets `self._memmap` never used; `self.count` unused except printing. Minor cruft: `self._memmap = None` — never set elsewhere. Remove? It's harmless but unused. Let me remove it for cleanliness. Also `self.count` is used in print. Keep count.

10. **`HybridIndex.build` — cache fingerprint mismatch prints "re-encoding" but doesn't delete old cache**: DenseIndex.build overwrites embeddings.fp16.npy with `open_memmap(mode="w+")` — recreates the file with new shape. What to measure:
- For each sampled S1 entity with non-empty ground truth, check which of its true matches appear in the retrieved candidate list at rank cutoffs K.
- recall@K = (sum over S1 of |truth ∩ top-K retrieved|) / (sum over S1 of |truth|). This is the micro recall — matches how train_model's `_candidate_recall` does it (found/total). I'll do the same for consistency.
- Also mean candidates per entity, and mean candidates at each K (trivially K, unless fewer available).
- Modes: lexical-only, dense-only, hybrid-merged. To measure all three in one run, I can build the HybridIndex once, and then for each batch compute:
  - lexical hits at lexical_k (from `lexical_retrieve_batch`)
  - dense hits at dense_k (from `index.dense.search(batch, dense_k)`)
  - merged via merge_hits
  Then compute recall@K on each of the three lists. That gives all three modes in one pass, no triple indexing.

But careful: recall@K for K > pool size is truncated (e.g., lexical pool = lexical_k=100, so recall@100 lexical is the max meaningful). For fair comparison, I should retrieve with generous pool sizes: lexical_k and dense_k should be >= max(K). Default ks = 10,25,50,60,100 → lexical_k default 100, dense_k default 100 for the evaluation. The user can override.

The query encoding cost is the same; the topk per chunk is k=100 instead of 40 — negligible difference. So default the eval to dense_k=100 but allow override.

Also the merged mode: merge_hits(lexical_hits, dense_hits, top_k). With top_k=100 the merged list has 100 entries. recall@K on merged for K ≤ 100.

```python
"""Recall measurement for candidate retrieval modes, before any matcher training.

Modes compared in one pass over a seeded sample of train S1 entities:

* lexical  - hash-index retrieval only (baseline)
* dense    - multilingual embedding top-k only
* hybrid   - reciprocal-rank fusion of both (what production ships)
* hybrid@top_k - the fused list truncated to the production size

Recall@K is micro-averaged over true match pairs of the sampled entities:
found / total, exactly the ceiling the downstream matcher can score.
Run with --no-dense for a lexical-only sanity check, or --cand-limit to
compare encoders on a candidate subsample (recall then drops artificially
and is only comparable across encoders, not to the full run).
"""
```

Implementation:

```python
def sample_s1(s1: pd.DataFrame, ground_truth: dict[str, set[str]], sample: int, seed: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    mask = s1["entity_id"].map(lambda entity_id: bool(ground_truth.get(entity_id)))
    matchable = s1[mask]
    if sample and sample < len(matchable):
        positions = np.random.default_rng(seed).choice(len(matchable), size=sample, replace=False)
        matchable = matchable.iloc[np.sort(positions)]
    print(f"[eval] Sampled {len(matchable):,} S1 entities with >=1 true match (of {mask.sum():,} matchable)")
    return matchable.reset_index(drop=True)
```

```python
def summarise(records, ks):
    names = list(records[0][2].keys()) if records else []
    summary = {}
    for name in names:
        found = {k: 0 for k in ks}
        total = 0
        cands = 0
        for _country, truth, modes in records:
            ids = modes[name]
            cands += len(ids)
            total += len(truth)
            id_set = set(ids)
            for k in ks:
                found[k] += sum(1 for tid in truth if tid in ids[:k])
        summary[name] = {
            "mean_candidates": cands / len(records) if records else 0.0,
            "recall": {k: found[k] / total if total else 0.0 for k in ks},
        }
    return summary
```

`tid in ids[:k]` — list membership O(k)... truth sets are small (1-5 ids), ids[:k] ≤ 100. Fine. Actually `ids[:k]` creates a slice each time — 4 modes × 5k entities × 5 Ks × small truths — trivial.

Per-country table:

```python
def per_country(records, mode, k):
    stats = defaultdict(lambda: [0, 0, 0])  # country -> [found, total, entities]
    for country, truth, modes in records:
        ids = modes[mode]
        stats[country][0] += sum(1 for tid in truth if tid in ids[:k])
        stats[country][1] += len(truth)
        stats[country][2] += 1
    return stats
```

Full code:

```python
"""Recall measurement for candidate retrieval, before any matcher training.

Measures, on a seeded sample of train S1 entities with known ground truth:

* lexical  - hash-index retrieval only (the baseline)
* dense    - multilingual embedding top-k only
* hybrid   - reciprocal-rank fusion of both pools, evaluated up to max K
* hybrid@<top_k> - exactly the list production would ship (production pools)

Recall@K is micro-averaged over true match pairs (found / total), the ceiling
the downstream matcher can score. Use --no-dense for a lexical-only baseline
and --cand-limit to compare encoders on a candidate subsample (recall then
drops artificially: only comparable across encoders, not to the full run).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import time
from collections import defaultdict

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from blocking import load_sources
from blocking import retrieve_batch as lexical_retrieve_batch
from hybrid_blocking import (
    DEFAULT_ENCODE_BATCH,
    DEFAULT_ENCODER,
    HybridIndex,
    iter_country_batches,
    merge_hits,
)
from preprocess import prepare_record


def load_ground_truth(path: str) -> dict[str, set[str]]:
    frame = pd.read_csv(path, sep="\t", dtype=str, keep_default_na=False)
    return {
        s1_id: set(matches.split(",")) if matches else set()
        for s1_id, matches in frame[["source1_entity_id", "matched_entity_ids"]].itertuples(index=False, name=None)
    }


def parse_ks(text: str) -> list[int]:
    return sorted({int(part) for part in text.split(",") if part.strip()})


def sample_s1(s1: pd.DataFrame, ground_truth: dict[str, set[str]], sample: int, seed: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    mask = s1["entity_id"].map(lambda entity_id: bool(ground_truth.get(entity_id)))
    matchable = s1[mask.reset_index(drop=True)]
```

Careful: s1["entity_id"].map returns a Series aligned to s1's index; s1 may have original index (loaded fresh → RangeIndex, fine). Use `s1[mask]` directly; mask has same index. OK.

```python
    matchable = s1[mask]
    if sample and sample < len(matchable):
        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        positions = np.sort(rng.choice(len(matchable), size=sample, replace=False))
        matchable = matchable.iloc[positions]
    print(f"[eval] Sampled {len(matchable):,} S1 entities with >=1 true match")
    return matchable.reset_index(drop=True)
```

Collect:

```python
def collect_records(
    s1_sample: pd.DataFrame,
    index: HybridIndex,
    ground_truth: dict[str, set[str]],
    candidate_ids: np.ndarray,
    ks: list[int],
    prod_lexical_k: int,
    prod_dense_k: int,
    prod_top_k: int,
    batch_size: int,
) -> tuple[list[tuple[str, set[str], dict[str, list[str]]]], float]:
    max_k = max(ks)
    eval_lex_k = max(prod_lexical_k, max_k)
    eval_dense_k = max(prod_dense_k, max_k)
    dense = index.dense
    records: list[tuple[str, set[str], dict[str, list[str]]]] = []
    started = time.time()
    processed = 0
    for batch in iter_country_batches(s1_sample, batch_size=batch_size):
        lexical = lexical_retrieve_batch(batch, index.lexical, top_k=eval_lex_k)
        dense_hits = dense.search(batch, eval_dense_k) if dense is not None else None
        for entity_id, name, address, country in batch[
            ["entity_id", "business_name", "business_address", "country"]
        ].itertuples(index=False, name=None):
            truth = ground_truth.get(entity_id, set())
            lex_hits = lexical.get(entity_id, [])
            modes: dict[str, list[str]] = {
                "lexical": [str(candidate_ids[hit.row]) for hit in lex_hits]
            }
            if dense_hits is not None:
                dense_list = dense_hits.get(entity_id, [])
                modes["dense"] = [str(candidate_ids[row]) for row, _score, _rank in dense_list]
                modes["hybrid"] = [
                    str(candidate_ids[hit.row])
                    for hit in merge_hits(lex_hits, dense_list, max_k)
                ]
                modes[f"hybrid@{prod_top_k}"] = [
                    str(candidate_ids[hit.row])
                    for hit in merge_hits(
                        lex_hits[:prod_lexical_k], dense_list[:prod_dense_k], prod_top_k
                    )
                ]
            records.append((prepare_record(name, address, country)["country"], truth, modes))
        processed += len(batch)
        print(f"[eval] Retrieved for {processed:,}/{len(s1_sample):,} sampled entities")
    return records, time.time() - started
```

Wait — `merge_hits(lex_hits[:prod_lexical_k], ...)`: lex_hits came from retrieve with top_k=eval_lex_k ≥ prod_lexical_k, ranked. Slicing to prod pool = production retrieval. dense_list ranked by rank. 

Note: `modes[f"hybrid@{prod_top_k}"]` — mode key with embedded k. In printing I'll reference it as prod_mode = f"hybrid@{prod_top_k}".

Summarise + per-country:

```python
def summarise(records, ks):
    names = list(records[0][2].keys()) if records else []
    summary = {}
    for name in names:
        found = {k: 0 for k in ks}
        total = 0
        candidates = 0
        for _country, truth, modes in records:
            ids = modes[name]
            candidates += len(ids)
            total += len(truth)
            for k in ks:
                prefix = ids[:k]
                found[k] += sum(1 for tid in truth if tid in prefix)
        summary[name] = {
            "mean_candidates": round(candidates / len(records), 1) if records else 0.0,
            "recall": {k: (found[k] / total if total else 0.0) for k in ks},
        }
    return summary
```

Per-country:

```python
def per_country_stats(records, mode: str, k: int) -> dict[str, tuple[int, int, int]]:
    stats: dict[str, list[int]] = defaultdict(lambda: [0, 0, 0])
    for country, truth, modes in records:
        ids = modes[mode][:k]
        entry = stats[country]
        entry[0] += sum(1 for tid in truth if tid in ids)
        entry[1] += len(truth)
        entry[2] += 1
    return {country: tuple(entry) for country, entry in stats.items()}
```

```python
def print_table(summary, ks):
    header = f"{'mode':<24}{'cands/entity':>14}" + "".join(f"{'R@' + str(k):>9}" for k in ks)
    print("\n" + header)
    for name, stats in summary.items():
        row = f"{name:<24}{stats['mean_candidates']:>14.1f}"
        row += "".join(f"{stats['recall'][k]:>9.4f}" for k in ks)
        print(row)
```

```python
def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Measure candidate recall@K for lexical / dense / hybrid retrieval."
    )
    parser.add_argument("--data-dir", default="dataset/train")
    parser.add_argument("--model-dir", default="models")
    parser.add_argument("--sample", type=int, default=3000)
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42)
    parser.add_argument("--ks", default="10,25,50,60,100")
    parser.add_argument("--top-k", type=int, default=60)
    parser.add_argument("--lexical-k", type=int, default=100)
    parser.add_argument("--dense-k", type=int, default=40)
    parser.add_argument("--encoder", default=DEFAULT_ENCODER)
    parser.add_argument("--device", default="auto")
    parser.add_argument("--encode-batch", type=int, default=DEFAULT_ENCODE_BATCH)
    parser.add_argument("--no-dense", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--cand-limit", type=int, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=1000)
    parser.add_argument("--save", default=None)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    ks = parse_ks(args.ks)
    s1, s2, s3 = load_sources(args.data_dir)
    candidates = pd.concat([s2, s3], ignore_index=True)
    if args.cand_limit is not None:
        candidates = candidates.head(args.cand_limit).copy()
        print(f"[eval] cand_limit={args.cand_limit}: recall is NOT comparable to the full run")
    candidate_ids = candidates["entity_id"].to_numpy(copy=False)
    ground_truth = load_ground_truth(os.path.join(args.data_dir, "train_ground_truth.tsv"))
    sample = sample_s1(s1, ground_truth, args.sample, args.seed)

    build_started = time.time()
    index = HybridIndex.build(
        candidates, args.data_dir, model_dir=args.model_dir, top_k=args.top_k,
        lexical_k=args.lexical_k, dense_k=args.dense_k, encoder=args.encoder,
        device=args.device, encode_batch=args.encode_batch,
        dense_enabled=not args.no_dense, cand_limit=args.cand_limit,
    )
    build_seconds = time.time() - build_started
```

41	def load_ground_truth(path: str) -> dict[str, set[str]]:
42	    frame = pd.read_csv(path, sep="\t", dtype=str, keep_default_na=False)
43	    return {
44	        s1_id: set(matches.split(",")) if matches else set()
45	        for s1_id, matches in frame[["source1_entity_id", "matched_entity_ids"]].itertuples(index=False, name=None)
46	    }

49	def _select_hard_negatives(labels: np.ndarray, source_ids: list[str]) -> np.ndarray:
50	    """Keep all positives and the highest-ranked retrieved negatives per S1."""
51	    keep: list[int] = []
52	    start = 0
53	    while start < len(labels):
54	        end = start + 1
55	        while end < len(labels) and source_ids[end] == source_ids[start]:
56	            end += 1
57	        group = np.arange(start, end)
58	        positive = group[labels[group] == 1]
59	        negative = group[labels[group] == 0]
60	        keep.extend(positive.tolist())
61	        # Candidate hits are emitted in retrieval-rank order. Singleton examples
62	        # retain negatives too, teaching the matcher that a plausible candidate
63	        # does not necessarily imply a real match.
64	        keep_negatives = min(len(negative), max(3, min(10, 5 * len(positive))))
65	        keep.extend(negative[:keep_negatives].tolist())
66	        start = end
67	    return np.asarray(keep, dtype=np.int64)
68	
69	
70	def _candidate_recall(
71	    hits_by_s1,
72	    ground_truth: dict[str, set[str]],
73	    candidate_ids: np.ndarray,
74	    ks: tuple[int, ...] = (25, 50, 100),
75	) -> tuple[dict[int, float], int, int]:
76	    found = {k: 0 for k in ks}
77	    total = 0
78	    for s1_id, hits in hits_by_s1.items():
79	        truth = ground_truth.get(s1_id, set())
80	        total += len(truth)
81	        if not truth:
82	            continue
83	        ids = [str(candidate_ids[hit.row]) for hit in hits]
84	        for k in ks:
85	            found[k] += sum(match in ids[:k] for match in truth)
86	    return ({k: found[k] / total if total else 0.0 for k in ks}, sum(found.values()), total)
87	
88	
89	def _decision_predictions(
90	    source_ids: list[str], candidate_rows: list[int], probabilities: np.ndarray,
91	    candidate_ids: np.ndarray, first_threshold: float, additional_threshold: float,
92	) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
93	    grouped: dict[str, list[tuple[float, int]]] = defaultdict(list)
94	    for s1_id, row, probability in zip(source_ids, candidate_rows, probabilities):
95	        grouped[s1_id].append((float(probability), row))
96	    predictions: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
97	    for s1_id, pairs in grouped.items():
98	        pairs.sort(reverse=True)
99	        if not pairs or pairs[0][0] < first_threshold:
100	            predictions[s1_id] = []
101	            continue
102	        accepted = [str(candidate_ids[row]) for score, row in pairs if score >= additional_threshold]
103	        if str(candidate_ids[pairs[0][1]]) not in accepted:
104	            accepted.insert(0, str(candidate_ids[pairs[0][1]]))
105	        predictions[s1_id] = accepted
106	    return predictions

41	def load_ground_truth(path: str) -> dict[str, set[str]]:
42	    frame = pd.read_csv(path, sep="\t", dtype=str, keep_default_na=False)
43	    return {

49	def _select_hard_negatives(labels: np.ndarray, source_ids: list[str]) -> np.ndarray:
50	    """Keep all positives and the highest-ranked retrieved negatives per S1."""
51	    keep: list[int] = []
52	    start = 0
53	    while start < len(labels):
54	        end = start + 1
55	        while end < len(labels) and source_ids[end] == source_ids[start]:
56	            end += 1
57	        group = np.arange(start, end)
58	        positive = group[labels[group] == 1]
59	        negative = group[labels[group] == 0]
60	        keep.extend(positive.tolist())
61	        # Candidate hits are emitted in retrieval-rank order. Singleton examples
62	        # retain negatives too, teaching the matcher that a plausible candidate
63	        # does not necessarily imply a real match.
64	        keep_negatives = min(len(negative), max(3, min(10, 5 * len(positive))))
65	        keep.extend(negative[:keep_negatives].tolist())
66	        start = end
67	    return np.asarray(keep, dtype=np.int64)
68	
69	
70	def _candidate_recall(
71	    hits_by_s1,
72	    ground_truth: dict[str, set[str]],
73	    candidate_ids: np.ndarray,
74	    ks: tuple[int, ...] = (25, 50, 100),
75	) -> tuple[dict[int, float], int, int]:
76	    found = {k: 0 for k in ks}
77	    total = 0
78	    for s1_id, hits in hits_by_s1.items():
79	        truth = ground_truth.get(s1_id, set())
80	        total += len(truth)
81	        if not truth:
82	            continue
83	        ids = [str(candidate_ids[hit.row]) for hit in hits]
84	        for k in ks:
85	            found[k] += sum(match in ids[:k] for match in truth)
86	    return ({k: found[k] / total if total else 0.0 for k in ks}, sum(found.values()), total)
87	
88	
89	def _decision_predictions(
90	    source_ids: list[str], candidate_rows: list[int], probabilities: np.ndarray,
91	    candidate_ids: np.ndarray, first_threshold: float, additional_threshold: float,
92	) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
93	    grouped: dict[str, list[tuple[float, int]]] = defaultdict(list)
94	    for s1_id, row, probability in zip(source_ids, candidate_rows, probabilities):
95	        grouped[s1_id].append((float(probability), row))
96	    predictions: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
97	    for s1_id, pairs in grouped.items():
98	        pairs.sort(reverse=True)
99	        if not pairs or pairs[0][0] < first_threshold:
100	            predictions[s1_id] = []
101	            continue
102	        accepted = [str(candidate_ids[row]) for score, row in pairs if score >= additional_threshold]
103	        if str(candidate_ids[pairs[0][1]]) not in accepted:
104	            accepted.insert(0, str(candidate_ids[pairs[0][1]]))
105	        predictions[s1_id] = accepted
106	    return predictions
107

109	def optimise_thresholds(
110	    source_ids: list[str], candidate_rows: list[int], probabilities: np.ndarray,
111	    candidate_ids: np.ndarray, ground_truth: dict[str, set[str]], validation_ids: list[str],
112	) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
113	    first_grid = np.arange(0.45, 0.96, 0.05)
114	    best = (0.50, 0.70, -1.0)
115	    for first in first_grid:
116	        for additional in np.arange(first, 0.991, 0.05):
117	            predictions = _decision_predictions(
118	                source_ids, candidate_rows, probabilities, candidate_ids, float(first), float(additional)
119	            )
120	            score = compute_validation_f05(predictions, ground_truth, validation_ids)

131	    feature_chunks: list[np.ndarray] = []
132	    label_chunks: list[np.ndarray] = []
133	    all_source_ids: list[str] = []
134	    all_candidate_rows: list[int] = []
135	    recall_found = {k: 0.0 for k in ks}
136	    recall_total = 0
137

144	        recall_total += total

150	            continue

Today is the 25th, so start now if you're ready. Also: once you start, you're expected to do it in one sitting, the countdown does not pause.

42	**The actual problem, technical must-knows**
43	
44	1. Task: entity resolution. Match Source 1 (deduplicated reference) records against Source 2 and Source 3 records that refer to the same real business. One S1 entity can match zero, one, or many records.
45	
46	2. Files are TSV, not CSV. Read with `sep="\t"` explicitly or pandas silently mangles it into one column.
47	
48	3. Country field: training only has US and India. Test set adds France with zero training examples. Do not hardcode to {US, India}, your pipeline needs to generalize to an unseen country label.
49	
50	4. You produce two output files:
51	   - matching_results.tsv: your final matches, this is the only one scored on the leaderboard.
52	   - candidate_pairs.tsv: the candidate set from your blocking stage before final matching. Not scored, but every ID in matching_results.tsv must appear here or it signals a bug. They use this to audit your blocking recall separately.
53	
54	5. Hard format rules: every Source 1 test entity needs exactly one row, empty list for no match, no duplicate IDs, no self matches to Source 1, no IDs that don't exist in the test set. Fail these and your submission isn't even evaluated.
55	
56	6. There's a validator script, `utils/validate_submission.py`, stdlib only. Run it before every leaderboard upload. No excuse to burn a submission on a formatting error.
57	
58	7. Scoring is F_0.5, precision weighted 2x over recall, computed per Source 1 entity then macro averaged. Singletons count too: correctly predicting no match scores 1.0, wrongly predicting any match scores 0.0. Don't ignore singleton detection, it's free points if you get it right and a real penalty if you don't.
59	
60	8. Model constraint: final model must be MIT or Apache 2.0 licensed and 8B parameters or fewer. This kills using GPT-4/Claude API or any closed model as your matcher. If you use embeddings for semantic similarity, the embedding model itself needs to meet this license and size cap.
61	
62	9. Absolutely banned: external lookups. No geocoding APIs, no business registry APIs, no internet augmentation to resolve entities. This is enforced and reviewed, disqualification risk is real, not a formality.
63	
64	10. Final submission isn't just the leaderboard upload. You need a full zip: output files, a runnable code folder with README and requirements.txt, and a filled methodology doc. Top teams get this reviewed in detail. Don't leave this for the last hour.
65	
66	11. Team size is 2 to 4. Confirm your teammates are locked in before you start the clock, since you can't add people mid-assessment.
67	
68	Given your CGPA and the fact you're already deep in dev work, the actual ML modeling here (blocking plus classifier on string similarity features like Jaccard, Levenshtein, TF-IDF) is not the hard part. The format compliance and license constraint are where teams lose easy points. Read the whole PDF once, fully, before you click Start, not after.

192	- TSV format

If your machine chokes, the AWS free tier credits are free compute you already qualify for. That's the only real reason to touch Builder Center now, convenience, not obligation.

226	Yes, this will run fine on your Infinix GT Book. i5-12500H, RTX 3050 6GB VRAM, 16GB DDR5.
227	
228	Reality check on what you actually need to train:
229	
230	**The core task doesn't need a GPU-heavy model.** This is entity resolution: blocking plus a classifier over string similarity features (Jaccard, Levenshtein, TF-IDF cosine on names and addresses). That's classic ML, scikit-learn, XGBoost, LightGBM territory. Runs on CPU, trains in minutes, your i5-12500H eats this alive.
231	
232	**Where the 8B parameter ceiling comes in:** If you use a transformer-based embedding model for semantic similarity (say a sentence-transformers model for fuzzy name/address matching beyond string metrics), 6GB VRAM is fine for inference and even light fine-tuning as long as you pick a small model. You are not training an 8B model from scratch, you'd be using one at most for embeddings or as a feature source, and most embedding models used for this kind of task are in the 100M to 1B range anyway. A full 8B model at fp16 needs roughly 16GB VRAM just to load, so if you're eyeing something that large, you'd quantize it or run it via CPU offload, but there's no reason this problem requires going anywhere near 8B params. The constraint is a ceiling, not a target.
233	
234	**Practical plan:** Do blocking with rule-based candidate generation (fuzzy matching, phonetic algorithms, TF-IDF nearest neighbor), do final matching with gradient-boosted trees on engineered similarity features. Your machine handles the entire pipeline without breaking a sweat. Save AWS credits as a backup if you decide to experiment with a heavier embedding model later, not because your laptop can't do the baseline approach.

236	User: So at any point 5 Get bottlenecked by my laptop Can I use aws builder centre from And I don't have to start from the scratch again right
237	
238	Claude: Yes to both, with conditions.
239	
240	**Can you use AWS Builder Center if bottlenecked:** Yes. It's free compute you already qualify for through registration. If your local training hits a wall (say a heavier embedding model choking your 6GB VRAM, or you want faster iteration), you spin up an instance there and keep going.
241	
242	**Do you have to start from scratch:** No, but it's not automatic either. You need to move things yourself:
243	
244	1. Your code (src/, scripts) — push to a private GitHub repo or just copy over. Trivial.
245	2. Your data — the dataset zip, upload it to the instance or to S3 and pull from there.
246	3. Any trained model checkpoints — scikit-learn/XGBoost models save as pickled files (.pkl, .joblib), embedding models save as standard checkpoint files. Copy these over and you resume exactly where you left off, no retraining needed.
247	4. Your Python environment — this is the part people forget. Your requirements.txt needs to match, or you reinstall the same package versions on the cloud instance. If you skip this and versions drift, you can hit silent bugs (different sklearn version giving slightly different results) or outright crashes.
248	
249	**The real cost isn't retraining, it's setup time.** Spinning up an instance, installing dependencies, transferring data, that's 20 to 40 minutes of friction depending on dataset size and your familiarity with the AWS console. Given you have a 72 hour window, that's not nothing.
250	
251	**My actual advice given your hardware:** Don't wait until you're bottlenecked to figure out the AWS setup. Do a dry run today: get an instance up, confirm your code runs there with a small subset of data, then tear it down. That way if you do hit a local wall on day 2, switching is a 5 minute data sync, not a first-time AWS learning curve eating into your hackathon time. You attended, or at least had access to, that Best Practices session on the 21st that walked through exactly this setup, worth checking if you saved that recording or the resources from it.

255	Claude: No, not required by the challenge rules. Nothing in the problem statement or guidelines says you must use GitHub or any version control platform. The only code requirement is that your final zip has a runnable `code/business_entity_resolution/src/` folder with README and requirements.txt.
256	
257	But practically, given what we just discussed, yes, set one up. Here's why it matters for you specifically:
258	
259	**For the laptop-to-AWS sync problem:** A private repo is the cleanest way to move code between your local machine and an AWS instance. `git push` locally, `git pull` on the instance, done. No manually copying files over SFTP or zipping things up each time you switch environments.
260	
261	**For team collaboration:** You said "team leader" earlier, meaning you have teammates. If more than one person is writing code, a repo isn't optional in practice, it's how you avoid overwriting each other's work or losing track of whose version is current.
262	
263	**"Simultaneously" specifically:** If you mean pushing from laptop and pulling on AWS at the same time as active development, that's normal git workflow, not a special setup. Just don't edit the same files in both places without pulling first, or you'll fight merge conflicts mid-hackathon which wastes time you don't have.
264	
265	One thing to flag: keep the repo private. You have a "strictly no external lookup" fair-play rule and a code review at the end, no reason to make your entity resolution approach public where a competing team could see it before judging. GitHub free tier gives you private repos, no cost concern there.

311	3. The Problem Statement
312	3.1 Task
313	Source 1 is the deduplicated reference source.
314	Sources 2 and 3 are noisy, independently collected sources.
315	For each Source 1 entity, find all matching records from Source 2 and Source 3.
316	A Source 1 entity may match zero, one, or many records from Source 2/3.
317	3.2 Data Fields
318	Each source file (`*_source1.tsv`, `*_source2.tsv`, `*_source3.tsv`) has these columns:
319	Column	Description
320	`entity_id`	Unique ID. Prefix indicates source: `S1-`, `S2-`, `S3-`
321	`business_name`	Name of the business (noisy)
322	`business_address`	Address (noisy, may be partial)
323	`country`	Country label. Training: US and India only. Test: also includes France (zero-shot).
324	> **Critical:** There is NO separate source column. Source is identified ONLY by the `entity_id` prefix and the file it came from.
325	3.3 Ground Truth File
326	`train_ground_truth.tsv` has two columns:
327	Column	Description
328	`source1_entity_id`	Entity ID of a Source 1 record
329	`matched_entity_ids`	Comma-separated list of matching S2/S3 IDs (empty if no matches)
330	3.4 Noise Patterns to Expect
331	Name variations: Abbreviations (Corp vs. Corporation, Pvt vs. Private, Ltd vs. Limited), DBA/trade names, punctuation differences (& vs. "and"), word-order transpositions, typos
332	Address variations: Abbreviations (Rd vs. Road, St vs. Street), transliteration variants, missing components (no PIN code, no state), landmark-based references (e.g., "Near SBI ATM"), component reordering

383	These rules apply to BOTH output files. Violations = submission rejected, not evaluated.

385	Every Source 1 entity must have exactly one row. Missing entities = rejection.

389	IDs in lists must only be S2- or S3- IDs that exist in the test set. No S1- IDs (no self-matches). No IDs not in the test set.
390	Every ID in `matching_results.tsv` must also appear in `candidate_pairs.tsv`. A matched ID that was never a candidate = pipeline bug, validator warns.
391	France test entities must appear in your submission. Do not hardcode, filter, or one-hot encode `country` to only `{US, India}`.
392	---
393	7. Validation Script
394	Run before EVERY leaderboard upload to catch format errors locally:
395	```bash
396	python3 utils/validate_submission.py \
397	    --matching output/matching_results.tsv \
398	    --candidate output/candidate_pairs.tsv \
399	    --test-dir dataset/test
400	```
401	Uses Python stdlib only, no dependencies.
402	Prints `PASS` (exit 0) when safe to submit.
403	Prints a numbered issue list (exit 1) if there are problems.
404	Does NOT compute your score — only checks format.
405	Submissions that fail validation are not evaluated at all. You won't even get a SCORED status.
406	---
407	8. Scoring Metric
408	F₀.₅ Score (precision-weighted):
409	$$F_{0.5} = \frac{1.25 \times \text{Precision} \times \text{Recall}}{0.25 \times \text{Precision} + \text{Recall}}$$
410	Precision is weighted 2× over recall. False merges (matching two different businesses) are penalized more than missed links.
411	Computed per Source 1 entity, then macro-averaged across all Source 1 entities.
412	Singletons are included in the average:
413	Correctly predicting empty match for a true singleton = 1.0 for that entity.
414	Predicting any match for a true singleton = 0.0 for that entity.
415	Example:
416	Predicted: `[S2-00047, S2-00193, S3-00812]`
417	Ground truth: `[S2-00047, S3-00812]`
418	Precision = 2/3 ≈ 0.667, Recall = 2/2 = 1.0
419	F₀.₅ = (1.25 × 0.667 × 1.0) / (0.25 × 0.667 + 1.0) = 0.714
420	---

423	Public	During the challenge (live)	A subset of the test set
424	Private	After the challenge ends	The remaining portion of the test set
425	Final rankings are based on the private leaderboard only.
426	You always submit predictions for the full test set. The split happens on Amazon's end.
427	Tiebreaker: Same score → earlier submission time ranks higher.
428	Max submissions: 5 per day during the hackathon.

502	15. Recommended Pipeline Architecture
503	```
504	Raw TSV Files
505	     ↓
506	[BLOCKING / CANDIDATE GENERATION STAGE]
507	  → generates candidate_pairs.tsv
508	  - For each S1 entity, find ~20–100 plausible S2/S3 candidates
509	  - Techniques: TF-IDF cosine similarity, MinHash LSH, character n-grams, BM25
510	  - Goal: HIGH RECALL (don't miss true matches — sets the recall ceiling)
511	     ↓
512	[MATCHING / SCORING MODEL]
513	  → generates matching_results.tsv
514	  - Score each candidate pair (S1 vs S2/S3 candidate)
515	  - Feature ideas: Levenshtein distance, Jaccard similarity, TF-IDF cosine, token sort ratio
516	  - Model options: XGBoost, LightGBM, small fine-tuned BERT (≤8B params, MIT/Apache 2.0)
517	  - Binary decision: match or not
518	  - Goal: HIGH PRECISION (F₀.₅ penalizes false positives 2×)
519	     ↓
520	[VALIDATION]
521	  - Run utils/validate_submission.py → must print PASS
522	     ↓
523	[UPLOAD]
524	  - Upload matching_results.tsv to Unstop portal (max 5/day)
525	```
526	Tips from the Problem Statement:
527	Invest heavily in blocking — it determines the upper bound of your recall
528	Explore string similarity features: Jaccard, Levenshtein, TF-IDF cosine
529	Pay attention to country-specific address patterns
530	Do NOT neglect singletons — correctly predicting "no match" earns a full 1.0
531	Consider the precision-recall trade-off carefully — F₀.₅ rewards precision more

1	"""Dense retrieval for candidate generation using FAISS and sentence-transformers."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	import argparse
6	import os
7	from dataclasses import dataclass
8	from pathlib import Path
9	
10	import faiss
11	import numpy as np
12	import pandas as pd
13	import torch
14	from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer
15	
16	from preprocess import prepare_record
17	
18	DEFAULT_TOP_K = 25
19	MAX_BLOCK_SIZE = 150
20	INDEX_PROGRESS_EVERY = 500_000
21	
22	@dataclass(frozen=True)
23	class CandidateHit:
24	    row: int
25	    retrieval_score: float
26	    pass_count: int
27	    best_rank: int
28	
29	
30	def load_sources(data_dir: str, s1_limit: int | None = None) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
31	    prefix = Path(data_dir).name
32	    read_kwargs = {"sep": "\t", "dtype": str, "keep_default_na": False}
33	    s1 = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(data_dir, f"{prefix}_source1.tsv"), **read_kwargs)
34	    s2 = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(data_dir, f"{prefix}_source2.tsv"), **read_kwargs)
35	    s3 = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(data_dir, f"{prefix}_source3.tsv"), **read_kwargs)
36	    if s1_limit is not None:
37	        s1 = s1.head(s1_limit).copy()
38	        print(f"[blocking] s1_limit={s1_limit}: using {len(s1):,} S1 rows")
39	    print(f"[blocking] Loaded: S1={len(s1):,}, S2={len(s2):,}, S3={len(s3):,} rows from '{data_dir}'")
40	    return s1, s2, s3
41	
42	@dataclass
43	class CandidateIndex:
44	    index: faiss.Index
45	    model: SentenceTransformer
46	    countries: np.ndarray
47	
48	    @classmethod
49	    def build(cls, candidates: pd.DataFrame) -> "CandidateIndex":
50	        n_rows = len(candidates)
51	        print(f"[blocking] Building dense retrieval FAISS index for {n_rows:,} S2/S3 records ...")
52	        
53	        device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
54	        model_name = "all-MiniLM-L6-v2"
55	        print(f"[blocking] Loading SentenceTransformer model '{model_name}' on {device}...")
56	        model = SentenceTransformer(model_name, device=device)
57	        
58	        texts = []
59	        countries = np.empty(n_rows, dtype=object)
60	        
61	        # Batch preparation
62	        rows = candidates[["business_name", "business_address", "country"]].itertuples(index=False, name=None)
63	        for row_idx, (name, address, country) in enumerate(rows):
64	            prepared = prepare_record(name, address, country)
65	            countries[row_idx] = str(prepared["country"])
66	            
67	            text = f"{prepared['name_core']} {prepared['name_core']} {prepared['addr_norm']} {prepared['country']}".strip()
68	            texts.append(text)
69	            
70	        print("[blocking] Encoding candidates...")
71	        embeddings = model.encode(texts, batch_size=512, show_progress_bar=True, normalize_embeddings=True)
72	        
73	        print("[blocking] Building FAISS index...")
74	        d = embeddings.shape[1]
75	        index = faiss.IndexFlatIP(d)
76	        
77	        if device == "cuda":
78	            res = faiss.StandardGpuResources()
79	            index = faiss.index_cpu_to_gpu(res, 0, index)
80	            
81	        index.add(embeddings)
82	        print("[blocking] Candidate index ready.")
83	        return cls(index=index, model=model, countries=countries)
84	
85	
86	def retrieve_batch(s1_batch: pd.DataFrame, index: CandidateIndex, top_k: int = DEFAULT_TOP_K) -> dict[str, list[CandidateHit]]:
87	    texts = []
88	    rows = s1_batch[["business_name", "business_address", "country"]].itertuples(index=False, name=None)
89	    countries = []
90	    for (name, address, country) in rows:
91	        prepared = prepare_record(name, address, country)
92	        countries.append(str(prepared["country"]))
93	        text = f"{prepared['name_core']} {prepared['name_core']} {prepared['addr_norm']} {prepared['country']}".strip()
94	        texts.append(text)
95	        
96	    embeddings = index.model.encode(texts, batch_size=len(texts), show_progress_bar=False, normalize_embeddings=True)
97	    
98	    scores, indices = index.index.search(embeddings, top_k * 2) # Retrieve more to filter by country boost
99	    
100	    result: dict[str, list[CandidateHit]] = {}
101	    for i, s1_id in enumerate(s1_batch["entity_id"]):
102	        query_country = countries[i]
103	        
104	        # apply country boost and rerank
105	        candidate_scores = []
106	        for j in range(indices.shape[1]):
107	            row_idx = int(indices[i][j])
108	            if row_idx < 0:
109	                continue
110	            
111	            score = float(scores[i][j])
112	            if query_country and query_country == index.countries[row_idx]:
113	                score += 0.2 # Boost matches in same country
114	                
115	            candidate_scores.append((row_idx, score))
116	            
117	        # Sort by boosted score
118	        candidate_scores.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
119	        
120	        hits = []
121	        for rank, (row_idx, score) in enumerate(candidate_scores[:top_k], start=1):
122	            hits.append(CandidateHit(row=row_idx, retrieval_score=score, pass_count=1, best_rank=rank))
123	            
124	        result[s1_id] = hits
125	        
126	    return result
127	
128	def candidate_ids(hits: list[CandidateHit], candidate_entity_ids: np.ndarray) -> list[str]:
129	    return [str(candidate_entity_ids[hit.row]) for hit in hits]
130	
131	def run_blocking(data_dir: str, output_path: str, top_k: int = DEFAULT_TOP_K, s1_limit: int | None = None) -> None:
132	    s1, s2, s3 = load_sources(data_dir, s1_limit=s1_limit)
133	    candidates = pd.concat([s2, s3], ignore_index=True)
134	    entity_ids = candidates["entity_id"].to_numpy(copy=False)
135	    index = CandidateIndex.build(candidates)
136	    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(output_path)), exist_ok=True)
137	    with open(output_path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
138	        handle.write("source1_entity_id\tcandidate_entity_ids\n")
139	        for start in range(0, len(s1), 2_000):
140	            batch = s1.iloc[start:start + 2_000]
141	            hits_by_s1 = retrieve_batch(batch, index, top_k=top_k)
142	            for s1_id in batch["entity_id"]:
143	                ids = candidate_ids(hits_by_s1[s1_id], entity_ids)
144	                handle.write(f"{s1_id}\t{','.join(ids)}\n")
145	            print(f"[blocking] Retrieved candidates for {min(start + len(batch), len(s1)):,}/{len(s1):,} S1 rows")
146	
147	if __name__ == "__main__":
148	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Generate ranked entity-resolution candidates")
149	    parser.add_argument("--data-dir", default="dataset/test")
150	    parser.add_argument("--output", default="output/candidate_pairs.tsv")
151	    parser.add_argument("--top-k", type=int, default=DEFAULT_TOP_K)
152	    parser.add_argument("--s1-limit", type=int, default=None)
153	    args = parser.parse_args()
154	    run_blocking(args.data_dir, args.output, args.top_k, args.s1_limit)

46	    (re.compile(r"\brd\b"), "road"), (re.compile(r"\bst\b"), "street"),
47	    (re.compile(r"\bave?\b"), "avenue"), (re.compile(r"\bblvd\b"), "boulevard"),
48	    (re.compile(r"\bdr\b"), "drive"), (re.compile(r"\bln\b"), "lane"),
49	    (re.compile(r"\bct\b"), "court"), (re.compile(r"\bpl\b"), "place"),
50	    (re.compile(r"\bsq\b"), "square"), (re.compile(r"\bpkwy\b"), "parkway"),
51	    (re.compile(r"\bhwy\b"), "highway"), (re.compile(r"\bapt\b|\bappt\b"), "apartment"),
52	    (re.compile(r"\bste\b"), "suite"), (re.compile(r"\bflr?\b"), "floor"),
53	    (re.compile(r"\bbldg\b"), "building"), (re.compile(r"\bno\b"), "number"),
54	)

56	_SPACE = re.compile(r"\s+")
57	_PUNCT = re.compile(r"[^\w\s\-']", flags=re.UNICODE)
58	_NUMBERS = re.compile(r"\d+")
59	_ALNUM = re.compile(r"[^\w]+", flags=re.UNICODE)
60	_STOP_TOKENS = frozenset({
61	    "the", "and", "of", "for", "company", "corporation", "incorporated",
62	    "limited", "private", "service", "services", "group", "road", "street",
63	    "avenue", "building", "india", "france", "usa", "united", "states",
64	})

67	def _unicode_safe(text: str) -> str:
68	    """Normalise Unicode without deleting predominantly non-Latin text."""
69	    text = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", text)
70	    ascii_text = text.encode("ascii", "ignore").decode("ascii").strip()
71	    if text.strip() and len(ascii_text) >= len(text.strip()) * 0.5:
72	        return ascii_text
73	    return "".join(
74	        char for char in text
75	        if unicodedata.category(char) not in {"Cs", "Cc", "Co"}
76	    )
77	
78	
79	@lru_cache(maxsize=500_000)
80	def clean_text(text: str) -> str:
81	    if not isinstance(text, str) or not text.strip():
82	        return ""
83	    text = _unicode_safe(text).lower()
84	    text = re.sub(r"\s*&\s*", " and ", text)
85	    text = _PUNCT.sub(" ", text)
86	    return _SPACE.sub(" ", text).strip()
87	
88	
89	@lru_cache(maxsize=500_000)
90	def normalize_business_name(name: str) -> str:
91	    text = clean_text(name)
92	    for pattern, replacement in NAME_REPLACEMENTS:
93	        text = pattern.sub(replacement, text)
94	    return _SPACE.sub(" ", text).strip()
95	
96	
97	@lru_cache(maxsize=500_000)
98	def normalize_address(address: str) -> str:
99	    text = clean_text(address)
100	    for pattern, replacement in ADDRESS_REPLACEMENTS:
101	        text = pattern.sub(replacement, text)
102	    return _SPACE.sub(" ", text).strip()
103	
104	
105	def name_core(name_normalized: str) -> str:
106	    """Remove only trailing legal-form tokens; retain the original form separately."""
107	    tokens = name_normalized.split()
108	    changed = True
109	    while tokens and changed:
110	        changed = False
111	        for phrase in LEGAL_SUFFIX_PHRASES:
112	            if len(tokens) >= len(phrase) and tuple(tokens[-len(phrase):]) == phrase:
113	                del tokens[-len(phrase):]
114	                changed = True
115	                break
116	        if not changed and tokens and tokens[-1] in LEGAL_SUFFIXES:
117	            tokens.pop()
118	            changed = True
119	    return " ".join(tokens)
120	
121	def legal_type(name_normalized: str) -> str:
122	    core = name_core(name_normalized)
123	    return name_normalized[len(core):].strip() if core else name_normalized
124	
125	
126	def compact_text(text: str) -> str:
127	    return _ALNUM.sub("", text)
128	
129	
130	def sorted_tokens(text: str) -> str:
131	    return " ".join(sorted(text.split()))
132	
133	
134	def initials(text: str) -> str:
135	    tokens = [token for token in text.split() if token not in _STOP_TOKENS and token]
136	    if len(tokens) == 1 and 2 <= len(tokens[0]) <= 8:
137	        return tokens[0]
138	    return "".join(token[0] for token in tokens)
139	
140	
141	def numeric_tokens(text: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
142	    return tuple(_NUMBERS.findall(text))
143	
144	
145	def significant_tokens(text: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
146	    tokens = [
147	        token for token in text.split()
148	        if len(token) >= 4 and not token.isdigit() and token not in _STOP_TOKENS
149	    ]
150	    return tuple(sorted(set(tokens), key=lambda token: (-len(token), token)))
151	
152	
153	def normalize_country(country: str) -> str:
154	    return clean_text(country)
155	
156	
157	def prepare_record(name: str, address: str, country: str) -> dict[str, object]:
158	    """Return compact representations used by retrieval and pair features."""
159	    raw_name = clean_text(name)
160	    raw_address = clean_text(address)
161	    norm_name = normalize_business_name(name)
162	    norm_address = normalize_address(address)
163	    core_name = name_core(norm_name)
164	    return {
165	        "name_raw": raw_name,
166	        "addr_raw": raw_address,
167	        "name_norm": norm_name,
168	        "name_core": core_name,
169	        "name_compact": compact_text(core_name),
170	        "name_sorted": sorted_tokens(core_name),
171	        "name_initials": initials(core_name),
172	        "legal_type": legal_type(norm_name),
173	        "addr_norm": norm_address,
174	        "addr_compact": compact_text(norm_address),
175	        "addr_sorted": sorted_tokens(norm_address),
176	        "addr_numbers": numeric_tokens(norm_address),
177	        "name_tokens": significant_tokens(core_name),
178	        "addr_tokens": significant_tokens(norm_address),
179	        "country": normalize_country(country),
180	    }
181	
182	
183	def make_combined_text(row) -> str:
184	    prepared = prepare_record(
185	        str(row.get("business_name", "") or ""),
186	        str(row.get("business_address", "") or ""),
187	        str(row.get("country", "") or ""),
188	    )
189	    return f"{prepared['name_core']} {prepared['name_core']} {prepared['addr_norm']}".strip()

26	def load_sources(data_dir: str, s1_limit: int | None = None) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:

39	def _fingerprint(value: str) -> np.uint64:
40	    """A process-local 64-bit key. Collisions are extraordinarily unlikely."""

65	@dataclass(frozen=True)
66	class CandidateHit:
67	    row: int
68	    retrieval_score: float
69	    pass_count: int
70	    best_rank: int
71	    # Hybrid retrieval populates these optional fields.  Keeping them on the
72	    # common hit object lets the pair model distinguish lexical evidence from
73	    # dense semantic similarity instead of treating both as one opaque score.

80	@dataclass
81	class SortedHashIndex:
82	    hashes: np.ndarray
83	    rows: np.ndarray
84	
85	    @classmethod
86	    def from_hashes(cls, raw_hashes: np.ndarray) -> "SortedHashIndex":
87	        order = np.argsort(raw_hashes, kind="stable")
88	        rows = order.astype(np.int32, copy=False)
89	        hashes = raw_hashes[order]
90	        return cls(hashes=hashes, rows=rows)
91	
92	    def lookup_hash(self, fingerprint: np.uint64, limit: int = MAX_BLOCK_SIZE) -> np.ndarray:
93	        left = int(np.searchsorted(self.hashes, fingerprint, side="left"))
94	        right = int(np.searchsorted(self.hashes, fingerprint, side="right"))
95	        size = right - left
96	        if size <= 0:
97	            return np.empty(0, dtype=np.int32)
98	        values = self.rows[left:right]
99	        if size <= limit:
100	            return values
101	        # A common key must not create an unbounded candidate pool. Spread the
102	        # deterministic sample across the full posting list instead of keeping
103	        # only the first rows.
104	        positions = np.linspace(0, size - 1, num=limit, dtype=np.int64)
105	        return values[positions]

108	@dataclass
109	class CandidateIndex:
110	    exact_name: SortedHashIndex

122	
123	    @classmethod
124	    def build(cls, candidates: pd.DataFrame) -> "CandidateIndex":
125	        n_rows = len(candidates)
126	        print(f"[blocking] Building bounded retrieval indexes for {n_rows:,} S2/S3 records ...")
127	        key_arrays = [np.empty(n_rows, dtype=np.uint64) for _ in range(11)]
128	        countries = np.empty(n_rows, dtype=object)
129	
130	        rows = candidates[["business_name", "business_address", "country"]].itertuples(index=False, name=None)
131	        for row_idx, (name, address, country) in enumerate(rows):
132	            prepared = prepare_record(name, address, country)
133	            country_value = str(prepared["country"])
134	            countries[row_idx] = country_value
135	            name_anchor = _anchor(prepared["name_tokens"])
136	            name_second_anchor = _second_anchor(prepared["name_tokens"])
137	            name_prefix = _prefix_anchor(prepared["name_tokens"])
138	            addr_anchor = _anchor(prepared["addr_tokens"])
139	            number = prepared["addr_numbers"][0] if prepared["addr_numbers"] else ""
140	            values = (
141	                str(prepared["name_norm"]),
142	                str(prepared["name_core"]),
143	                str(prepared["name_compact"]),
144	                str(prepared["name_sorted"]),
145	                str(prepared["addr_compact"]),
146	                name_anchor,
147	                name_second_anchor,
148	                name_prefix,
149	                addr_anchor,
150	                _numeric_key(number, addr_anchor),

152	            )
153	            for array, value in zip(key_arrays, values):
154	                array[row_idx] = _fingerprint(value)
155	            if (row_idx + 1) % INDEX_PROGRESS_EVERY == 0:
156	                print(f"[blocking]   indexed {row_idx + 1:,}/{n_rows:,} candidates")
157	
158	        # Pop each raw key array once it has been sorted so we do not hold the
159	        # complete unsorted and sorted index sets at the same time.
160	        indexes_reversed = []
161	        while key_arrays:
162	            indexes_reversed.append(SortedHashIndex.from_hashes(key_arrays.pop()))
163	        indexes = list(reversed(indexes_reversed))
164	        print("[blocking] Candidate indexes ready.")
165	        return cls(*indexes, countries=countries)

167	    def retrieve(self, name: str, address: str, country: str, top_k: int = DEFAULT_TOP_K) -> list[CandidateHit]:
168	        prepared = prepare_record(name, address, country)
169	        country_value = str(prepared["country"])
170	        name_anchor = _anchor(prepared["name_tokens"])
171	        name_second_anchor = _second_anchor(prepared["name_tokens"])
172	        name_prefix = _prefix_anchor(prepared["name_tokens"])
173	        addr_anchor = _anchor(prepared["addr_tokens"])
174	        number = prepared["addr_numbers"][0] if prepared["addr_numbers"] else ""
175	        queries = (
176	            ("exact", self.exact_name, str(prepared["name_norm"]), 100.0),
177	            ("core", self.core_name, str(prepared["name_core"]), 92.0),
178	            ("compact", self.compact_name, str(prepared["name_compact"]), 88.0),
179	            ("sorted", self.sorted_name, str(prepared["name_sorted"]), 84.0),
180	            ("address_exact", self.compact_address, str(prepared["addr_compact"]), 52.0),
181	            ("name_anchor", self.name_anchor, name_anchor, 45.0),
182	            ("name_second_anchor", self.name_second_anchor, name_second_anchor, 30.0),
183	            ("name_prefix", self.name_prefix, name_prefix, 24.0),
184	            ("address_anchor", self.address_anchor, addr_anchor, 30.0),
185	            ("numeric_address", self.numeric_address, _numeric_key(number, addr_anchor), 60.0),
186	            ("initials", self.initials, str(prepared["name_initials"]), 12.0),
187	        )
188	        scores: dict[int, list[float]] = {}
189	        for _pass_name, index, value, weight in queries:
190	            if not value:

192	            rows = index.lookup_hash(_fingerprint(value))
193	            for rank, row in enumerate(rows, start=1):
194	                item = scores.setdefault(int(row), [0.0, 0.0, float(rank)])
195	                item[0] += weight / np.log2(rank + 1.0)
196	                item[1] += 1.0
197	                item[2] = min(item[2], float(rank))

199	        # Country remains an open string feature. It boosts agreement without

201	        for row, values in scores.items():
202	            if country_value and country_value == self.countries[row]:
203	                values[0] += 8.0
204	
205	        ranked = sorted(scores.items(), key=lambda item: (-item[1][0], -item[1][1], item[1][2], item[0]))[:top_k]
206	        return [
207	            CandidateHit(row=row, retrieval_score=float(values[0]), pass_count=int(values[1]), best_rank=int(values[2]))
208	            for row, values in ranked

223	def run_blocking(data_dir: str, output_path: str, top_k: int = DEFAULT_TOP_K, s1_limit: int | None = None) -> None:

31	    "name_jaro_winkler", "name_token_jaccard", "name_initials_match",
32	    "name_legal_type_match", "name_length_ratio", "name_token_count_difference",

34	    "addr_token_set_ratio", "addr_token_jaccard", "addr_length_ratio",

36	    "country_match", "country_conflict", "country_missing_either",

42	def _tokens(value: str) -> set[str]:

46	def _jaccard(left: str, right: str) -> float:
47	    left_tokens, right_tokens = _tokens(left), _tokens(right)
48	    if not left_tokens and not right_tokens:
49	        return 1.0
50	    if not left_tokens or not right_tokens:
51	        return 0.0
52	    return len(left_tokens & right_tokens) / len(left_tokens | right_tokens)
53	
54	
55	def _length_ratio(left: str, right: str) -> float:
56	    longest = max(len(left), len(right))

60	def _number_features(left: tuple[str, ...], right: tuple[str, ...]) -> tuple[float, float, float, float]:
61	    left_set, right_set = set(left), set(right)
62	    if not left_set and not right_set:
63	        return 1.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0
64	    if not left_set or not right_set:
65	        return 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0
66	    overlap = len(left_set & right_set) / len(left_set | right_set)
67	    exact = float(left_set == right_set)
68	    # A fully disjoint number set is strong negative evidence. Partial mismatch
69	    # remains a softer signal because addresses can contain PINs and suites.
70	    conflict = float(not (left_set & right_set))
71	    count_diff = abs(len(left_set) - len(right_set)) / max(len(left_set), len(right_set), 1)
72	    return exact, overlap, conflict, count_diff

75	def _jaro_winkler(left: str, right: str) -> float:

78	    if not left or not right:

80	    if jellyfish is None:

94	    address_set = fuzz.token_set_ratio(str(left["addr_norm"]), str(right["addr_norm"])) / 100.0
95	    address_jaccard = _jaccard(str(left["addr_norm"]), str(right["addr_norm"]))
96	    numbers_exact, numbers_overlap, numbers_conflict, number_count_difference = _number_features(
97	        left["addr_numbers"], right["addr_numbers"]
98	    )
99	    country_left, country_right = str(left["country"]), str(right["country"])
100	    country_missing = float(not country_left or not country_right)
101	    country_match = float(bool(country_left) and country_left == country_right)
102	    country_conflict = float(bool(country_left and country_right and country_left != country_right))
103	    name_strong = float(name_set >= 0.90 or name_lev >= 0.94)
104	    address_strong = float(address_set >= 0.85 or numbers_exact == 1.0)
105	
106	    return np.array([
107	        float(left["name_raw"] == right["name_raw"] and bool(left["name_raw"])),
108	        float(left["name_norm"] == right["name_norm"] and bool(left["name_norm"])),
109	        float(left["name_core"] == right["name_core"] and bool(left["name_core"])),
110	        name_raw, name_lev, name_sort, name_set,
111	        _jaro_winkler(str(left["name_core"]), str(right["name_core"])),
112	        name_jaccard,
113	        float(bool(left["name_initials"]) and left["name_initials"] == right["name_initials"]),
114	        float(bool(left["legal_type"]) and left["legal_type"] == right["legal_type"]),
115	        _length_ratio(str(left["name_core"]), str(right["name_core"])),
116	        abs(len(str(left["name_core"]).split()) - len(str(right["name_core"]).split())) /
117	        max(len(str(left["name_core"]).split()), len(str(right["name_core"]).split()), 1),
118	        address_raw, address_lev, address_sort, address_set, address_jaccard,
119	        _length_ratio(str(left["addr_norm"]), str(right["addr_norm"])),
120	        numbers_exact, numbers_overlap, numbers_conflict, number_count_difference,
121	        country_match, country_conflict, country_missing,
122	        name_strong * address_strong, name_strong * numbers_conflict,
123	        min(hit.retrieval_score / 100.0, 2.0), min(hit.pass_count / 11.0, 1.0),
124	        1.0 / max(hit.best_rank, 1),
125	    ], dtype=np.float32)
126	
127	
128	def extract_features_for_hits(
129	    s1_batch,
130	    candidates,
131	    hits_by_s1: dict[str, list[CandidateHit]],
132	) -> tuple[np.ndarray, list[str], list[int], list[CandidateHit]]:
133	    """Build a feature matrix for one bounded Source 1 batch."""
134	    candidate_cache: dict[int, dict[str, Any]] = {}
135	    rows: list[np.ndarray] = []
136	    source_ids: list[str] = []
137	    candidate_rows: list[int] = []
138	    hits_out: list[CandidateHit] = []
139	
140	    for s1_id, name, address, country in s1_batch[["entity_id", "business_name", "business_address", "country"]].itertuples(index=False, name=None):
141	        left = prepare_record(name, address, country)
142	        for hit in hits_by_s1.get(s1_id, []):
143	            right = candidate_cache.get(hit.row)
144	            if right is None:
145	                candidate = candidates.iloc[hit.row]
146	                right = prepare_record(candidate.business_name, candidate.business_address, candidate.country)
147	                candidate_cache[hit.row] = right
148	            rows.append(extract_pair_features(left, right, hit))
149	            source_ids.append(s1_id)
150	            candidate_rows.append(hit.row)
151	            hits_out.append(hit)
152	
153	    if not rows:
154	        return np.empty((0, len(FEATURE_NAMES)), dtype=np.float32), [], [], []
155	    return np.vstack(rows), source_ids, candidate_rows, hits_out

31	def load_ground_truth(path: str) -> dict[str, set[str]]:
32	    frame = pd.read_csv(path, sep="\t", dtype=str, keep_default_na=False)
33	    return {
34	        s1_id: set(matches.split(",")) if matches else set()
