100	class DenseIndex:
101	    """Country-segmented exact top-k cosine index over an fp16 memmap cache."""
102	
103	    def __init__(self, cache_dir: str, encoder: str, device: str, encode_batch: int):
104	        self.cache_dir = cache_dir
105	        self.encoder = encoder
106	        self.encode_batch = encode_batch
107	        self.device = _resolve_device(device)
108	        self.device_is_cuda = self.device.startswith("cuda")
109	        self.dim: int = 0
110	        self.count: int = 0
111	        self.segments: dict[str, tuple[int, int]] = {}  # country -> (start, count)
112	        self.order: np.ndarray | None = None            # memmap position -> candidate row
113	        self._memmap = None
114	        self._model = None
115	
116	    # -- construction -----------------------------------------------------
117	
118	    @classmethod
119	    def build(
120	        cls,
121	        candidates: pd.DataFrame,
122	        texts_by_country: dict[int, list[str]],
123	        country_ids: np.ndarray,
124	        country_names: dict[int, str],
125	        cache_dir: str,
126	        encoder: str,
127	        device: str,
128	        encode_batch: int,
129	    ) -> "DenseIndex":
130	        """Encode texts (already grouped by country) into a fresh cache."""
131	        os.makedirs(cache_dir, exist_ok=True)
132	        index = cls(cache_dir, encoder, device, encode_batch)
133	        index._load_model()
134	
135	        n = len(candidates)
136	        order = np.argsort(country_ids, kind="stable")
137	        segments: dict[str, tuple[int, int]] = {}
138	        position = 0
139	        for cid in range(len(country_names)):
140	            count = len(texts_by_country[cid])
141	            if count:
142	                segments[country_names[cid]] = (position, count)
143	                position += count
144	
145	        print(f"[dense] Encoding {n:,} candidate texts on device '{index.device}' "
146	              f"(model={encoder}, dim={index.dim}) ...")
147	        memmap_path = os.path.join(cache_dir, "embeddings.fp16.npy")
148	        memmap = np.lib.format.open_memmap(memmap_path, mode="w+", dtype=np.float16, shape=(n, index.dim))
149	        for cid in range(len(country_names)):
150	            country = country_names[cid]
151	            start, count = segments.get(country, (0, 0))
152	            texts = texts_by_country[cid]
153	            for chunk_start in range(0, count, ENCODE_CHUNK):
154	                chunk = texts[chunk_start:chunk_start + ENCODE_CHUNK]
155	                vectors = index._encode_texts(chunk)
156	                memmap[start + chunk_start:start + chunk_start + len(chunk)] = vectors.astype(np.float16)
157	                done = min(chunk_start + len(chunk), count)
158	                print(f"[dense]   {country or '<empty>'}: encoded {done:,}/{count:,}")
159	            texts_by_country[cid] = None  # free the text list as we go
160	        memmap.flush()
161	        del memmap
162	
163	        order_path = os.path.join(cache_dir, "order.npy")
164	        np.save(order_path, order.astype(np.int64))
165	        meta = {
166	            "encoder": encoder,
167	            "text_version": ENCODER_TEXT_VERSION,
168	            "dim": index.dim,
169	            "count": n,
170	            "segments": {country: [int(s), int(c)] for country, (s, c) in segments.items()},
171	        }
172	        with open(os.path.join(cache_dir, "dense_meta.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
173	            json.dump(meta, handle, indent=2)
174	        index.order = order.astype(np.int64)
175	        index.segments = segments
176	        index.count = n
177	        print(f"[dense] Cache written to {cache_dir}")
178	        return index
179	
180	    @classmethod
181	    def load(cls, cache_dir: str, encoder: str, device: str, encode_batch: int) -> "DenseIndex | None":
182	        meta_path = os.path.join(cache_dir, "dense_meta.json")
183	        order_path = os.path.join(cache_dir, "order.npy")
184	        memmap_path = os.path.join(cache_dir, "embeddings.fp16.npy")
185	        if not (os.path.isfile(meta_path) and os.path.isfile(order_path) and os.path.isfile(memmap_path)):
186	            return None
187	        with open(meta_path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
188	            meta = json.load(handle)
189	        index = cls(cache_dir, meta["encoder"], device, encode_batch)
190	        index.dim = int(meta["dim"])
191	        index.count = int(meta["count"])
192	        index.segments = {country: (int(start), int(count)) for country, (start, count) in meta["segments"].items()}
193	        index.order = np.load(order_path)
194	        index._load_model()
195	        print(f"[dense] Reusing cached embeddings: {index.count:,} vectors, "
196	              f"{len(index.segments)} countries, dim={index.dim}")
197	        return index
198	
199	    def _load_model(self):
200	        if not HAVE_DENSE:
201	            raise RuntimeError("sentence-transformers/torch not installed; dense retrieval unavailable")
202	        print(f"[dense] Loading encoder '{self.encoder}' on device '{self.device}' ...")
203	        self._model = SentenceTransformer(self.encoder, device=self.device)
204	        if self.device_is_cuda:
205	            try:
206	                self._model.half()
207	            except Exception:
208	                pass
209	        if hasattr(self._model, "get_embedding_dimension"):
210	            self.dim = int(self._model.get_embedding_dimension())
211	        else:  # sentence-transformers < 5
212	            self.dim = int(self._model.get_sentence_embedding_dimension())
213	
214	    # -- search -----------------------------------------------------------
215	
216	    def _encode_texts(self, texts: list[str]) -> np.ndarray:
217	        vectors = self._model.encode(
218	            texts,
219	            batch_size=self.encode_batch,
220	            show_progress_bar=False,
221	            normalize_embeddings=True,
222	            convert_to_numpy=True,
223	        )
224	        return np.asarray(vectors, dtype=np.float32)
225	
226	    def _open_memmap(self) -> np.ndarray:
227	        if self._memmap is None:
228	            self._memmap = np.load(os.path.join(self.cache_dir, "embeddings.fp16.npy"), mmap_mode="r")
229	        return self._memmap
230	
231	    def search(self, s1_batch: pd.DataFrame, top_k: int) -> dict[str, list[tuple[int, float, int]]]:
232	        """Dense top-k per S1 entity: entity_id -> [(candidate row, cosine, rank)].
233	
234	        The country segment is streamed from the fp16 memmap in SEARCH_CHUNK
235	        blocks rather than loaded whole, so peak device memory is one chunk no
236	        matter how large the segment is. Each chunk is scored against every
237	        query of the country before the next chunk is fetched; repeated passes
238	        over a segment are served from the OS page cache.
239	        """
240	        if self._model is None:
241	            return {}
242	        groups: dict[str, list[tuple[str, str]]] = defaultdict(list)
243	        for entity_id, name, address, country in s1_batch[
244	            ["entity_id", "business_name", "business_address", "country"]
245	        ].itertuples(index=False, name=None):
246	            prepared = prepare_record(name, address, country)
247	            groups[str(prepared["country"])].append((entity_id, encoder_text(prepared)))
248	
249	        results: dict[str, list[tuple[int, float, int]]] = {}
250	        source = self._open_memmap()
251	        for country, items in groups.items():
252	            segment = self.segments.get(country)
253	            if segment is None:
254	                continue
255	            start, count = segment
256	            k = min(top_k, count)
257	            if k <= 0:
258	                continue
259	            dtype = torch.float16 if self.device_is_cuda else torch.float32
260	            queries = torch.from_numpy(
261	                self._encode_texts([text for _, text in items])
262	            ).to(device=self.device, dtype=dtype)
263	            group_bounds = [
264	                (offset, min(offset + QUERY_GROUP, len(items)))
265	                for offset in range(0, len(items), QUERY_GROUP)
266	            ]
267	            best: list[tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor] | None] = [None] * len(group_bounds)
268	            for chunk_start in range(0, count, SEARCH_CHUNK):
269	                chunk_end = min(chunk_start + SEARCH_CHUNK, count)
270	                block = np.array(source[start + chunk_start:start + chunk_end])
271	                chunk = torch.from_numpy(block).to(device=self.device, dtype=dtype)
272	                for group_index, (group_start, group_end) in enumerate(group_bounds):
273	                    sims = queries[group_start:group_end] @ chunk.t()
274	                    chunk_k = min(k, chunk_end - chunk_start)
275	                    scores_chunk, positions_chunk = torch.topk(sims, chunk_k, dim=1)
276	                    positions_chunk = positions_chunk + chunk_start
277	                    current = best[group_index]
278	                    if current is None:
279	                        best[group_index] = (scores_chunk, positions_chunk)
280	                        continue
281	                    scores, positions = current
282	                    scores = torch.cat([scores, scores_chunk], dim=1)
283	                    positions = torch.cat([positions, positions_chunk], dim=1)
284	                    if scores.shape[1] > k:
285	                        scores, merge_order = torch.topk(scores, k, dim=1)
286	                        positions = torch.gather(positions, 1, merge_order)
287	                    best[group_index] = (scores, positions)
288	                del chunk
289	            del queries
290	            if self.device_is_cuda:
291	                torch.cuda.empty_cache()
292	            print(f"[dense] Searched segment {country!r}: {count:,} vectors x {len(items):,} queries")
293	            for group_index, (group_start, group_end) in enumerate(group_bounds):
294	                scores, positions = best[group_index]
295	                scores_np = scores.float().cpu().numpy()
296	                positions_np = positions.cpu().numpy()
297	                for row_index in range(group_end - group_start):
298	                    entity_id = items[group_start + row_index][0]
299	                    hits = []
300	                    for rank in range(scores_np.shape[1]):
301	                        position = int(positions_np[row_index, rank])
302	                        candidate_row = int(self.order[start + position])
303	                        hits.append((candidate_row, float(scores_np[row_index, rank]), rank + 1))
304	                    results[entity_id] = hits
305	        return results
306	
307	
308	def merge_hits(
309	    lexical_hits: list[CandidateHit],
310	    dense_hits: list[tuple[int, float, int]],
311	    top_k: int,
312	) -> list[CandidateHit]:
313	    """Reciprocal-rank fusion of the two retrieval modes."""
314	    lexical_by_row = {hit.row: hit for hit in lexical_hits}
315	    dense_by_row = {row: (score, rank) for row, score, rank in dense_hits}
316	    fused: list[tuple[float, int, CandidateHit | None, float, int]] = []
317	    for row in set(lexical_by_row) | set(dense_by_row):
318	        lexical = lexical_by_row.get(row)
319	        dense_score, dense_rank = dense_by_row.get(row, (0.0, 0))
320	        score = 0.0
321	        if lexical is not None and lexical.lexical_rank:
322	            score += 1.0 / (RRF_K + lexical.lexical_rank)
323	        if dense_rank:
324	            score += 1.0 / (RRF_K + dense_rank)
325	        fused.append((score, row, lexical, dense_score, dense_rank))
326	    fused.sort(key=lambda item: (-item[0], item[1]))
327	    return [
328	        CandidateHit(
329	            row=row,
330	            retrieval_score=float(score),
331	            lexical_score=(lexical.lexical_score if lexical is not None else 0.0),
332	            lexical_pass_count=(lexical.lexical_pass_count if lexical is not None else 0),
333	            lexical_rank=(lexical.lexical_rank if lexical is not None else 0),
334	            dense_score=float(dense_score),
335	            dense_rank=int(dense_rank),
336	        )
337	        for score, row, lexical, dense_score, dense_rank in fused[:top_k]
338	    ]

342	    """Lexical index + optional dense index, merged per S1 entity."""

344	    def __init__(self, lexical: CandidateIndex, dense: DenseIndex | None,
345	                 top_k: int, lexical_k: int, dense_k: int):
346	        self.lexical = lexical
347	        self.dense = dense
348	        self.top_k = top_k
349	        self.lexical_k = lexical_k
350	        self.dense_k = dense_k

352	    @classmethod
353	    def build(

366	    ) -> "HybridIndex":

368	            candidates = candidates.head(cand_limit).copy()
369	            print(f"[hybrid] cand_limit={cand_limit}: using {len(candidates):,} candidate rows")
370	        if dense_enabled and not HAVE_DENSE:

375	        cache_dir = None

382	            fingerprint = _cache_fingerprint(source_paths(data_dir), encoder, cand_limit)
383	            meta_path = os.path.join(cache_dir, "dense_meta.json")
384	            if os.path.isfile(meta_path):

386	                    stored = json.load(handle)

390	                    dense_index = DenseIndex.load(cache_dir, encoder, device, encode_batch)
391	                else:

396	              f"(lexical_k={lexical_k}, dense_k={dense_k}, top_k={top_k}) ...")
397	        key_arrays = [np.empty(n_rows, dtype=np.uint64) for _ in range(11)]
398	        need_dense = dense_enabled and dense_index is None
399	        country_ids = np.empty(n_rows, dtype=np.int32) if need_dense else None

415	                texts_by_country[cid].append(encoder_text(prepared))
416	            if (row_idx + 1) % 500_000 == 0:

434	    def retrieve_batch(self, s1_batch: pd.DataFrame, top_k: int | None = None) -> dict[str, list[CandidateHit]]:
435	        top_k = self.top_k if top_k is None else top_k
436	        lexical = lexical_retrieve_batch(s1_batch, self.lexical, top_k=self.lexical_k)
437	        if self.dense is None:
438	            return {s1_id: hits[:top_k] for s1_id, hits in lexical.items()}
439	        dense = self.dense.search(s1_batch, self.dense_k)
440	        return {
441	            s1_id: merge_hits(lexical.get(s1_id, []), dense.get(s1_id, []), top_k)
442	            for s1_id in s1_batch["entity_id"]
443	        }

451	def iter_country_batches(s1: pd.DataFrame, batch_size: int = 1_000):
452	    """Yield S1 batches whose rows share one country (raw column value order).
453	
454	    Country-grouped iteration keeps each dense search() call inside a single
455	    country segment, so the memmap reads stay sequential and page-cache
456	    friendly.
457	    """
458	    if len(s1) == 0:
459	        return
460	    country_values = s1["country"].astype(str).to_numpy()
461	    order = np.argsort(country_values, kind="stable")
462	    sorted_s1 = s1.iloc[order]
463	    for start in range(0, len(sorted_s1), batch_size):
464	        yield sorted_s1.iloc[start:start + batch_size]

3	Retrieval strategy
4	------------------
5	1. Lexical pass (``blocking.CandidateIndex``): 11 country-prefixed hash indexes.
6	2. Dense pass (``DenseIndex``): multilingual sentence embeddings, exact top-k
7	   cosine search restricted to the query's country segment. The multilingual
8	   encoder is what makes cross-script matches (Devanagari candidate vs Latin
9	   source name) retrievable at all.
10	3. Merge: reciprocal-rank fusion; the fused top-k becomes the final candidate set.
11	
12	Memory model
13	------------
14	Dense embeddings never live fully in RAM. They are encoded once into an fp16
15	memmap cache on disk (per data directory, under ``<model_dir>/cache/``); at
16	search time each country segment is streamed through the compute device in
17	bounded SEARCH_CHUNK blocks, so peak device memory is one chunk (~200MB)
18	regardless of segment size (the largest country alone is 4.4GB fp16, which
19	fits neither a 6GB GPU next to the encoder nor spare RAM next to the source
20	DataFrames). There is no FAISS dependency: top-k is an exact matmul, which
21	also keeps results deterministic.
22	"""
23

58	DEFAULT_TOP_K = 60            # final merged candidates per S1 entity
59	DEFAULT_LEXICAL_K = 100       # lexical pool size before the merge
60	DEFAULT_DENSE_K = 40          # dense pool size before the merge
61	DEFAULT_ENCODER = "paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2"
62	DEFAULT_ENCODE_BATCH = 256
63	ENCODER_TEXT_VERSION = 1
64	ENCODE_CHUNK = 200_000        # texts per encode call (bounds the fp32 output array)
65	SEARCH_CHUNK = 250_000        # segment rows per matmul (bounds the sims matrix)
66	QUERY_GROUP = 256             # queries per matmul (bounds the sims matrix)
67	RRF_K = 60.0

70	def encoder_text(prepared: dict) -> str:
71	    """The text fed to the dense encoder; the name is repeated to weight it."""
72	    name = str(prepared["name_core"]) or str(prepared["name_raw"])
73	    return f"{name} {name} {prepared['addr_norm']}".strip()
74	
75	
76	def source_paths(data_dir: str) -> list[str]:
77	    prefix = Path(data_dir).name
78	    return [os.path.join(data_dir, f"{prefix}_source2.tsv"), os.path.join(data_dir, f"{prefix}_source3.tsv")]

81	def _cache_fingerprint(files: list[str], encoder: str, cand_limit: int | None) -> str:
82	    parts = [f"encoder={encoder}", f"text_version={ENCODER_TEXT_VERSION}", f"cand_limit={cand_limit}"]
83	    for path in files:
84	        if os.path.isfile(path):
85	            stat = os.stat(path)
86	            parts.append(f"{os.path.basename(path)}:{stat.st_size}:{int(stat.st_mtime)}")
87	        else:
88	            parts.append(f"{os.path.basename(path)}:missing")
89	    return hashlib.sha1("|".join(parts).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
90

92	def _resolve_device(device: str) -> str:
93	    if device != "auto":
94	        return device
95	    if torch is not None and torch.cuda.is_available():
96	        return "cuda"
97	    return "cpu"

100	class DenseIndex:
101	    """Country-segmented exact top-k cosine index over an fp16 memmap cache."""
102	
103	    def __init__(self, cache_dir: str, encoder: str, device: str, encode_batch: int):
104	        self.cache_dir = cache_dir
105	        self.encoder = encoder
106	        self.encode_batch = encode_batch
107	        self.device = _resolve_device(device)
108	        self.device_is_cuda = self.device.startswith("cuda")
109	        self.dim: int = 0
110	        self.count: int = 0
111	        self.segments: dict[str, tuple[int, int]] = {}  # country -> (start, count)
112	        self.order: np.ndarray | None = None            # memmap position -> candidate row
113	        self._memmap = None
114	        self._model = None
115	
116	    # -- construction -----------------------------------------------------
117	
118	    @classmethod
119	    def build(
120	        cls,
121	        candidates: pd.DataFrame,
122	        texts_by_country: dict[int, list[str]],
123	        country_ids: np.ndarray,
124	        country_names: dict[int, str],
125	        cache_dir: str,
126	        encoder: str,
127	        device: str,
128	        encode_batch: int,
129	    ) -> "DenseIndex":
130	        """Encode texts (already grouped by country) into a fresh cache."""
131	        os.makedirs(cache_dir, exist_ok=True)
132	        index = cls(cache_dir, encoder, device, encode_batch)
133	        index._load_model()
134	
135	        n = len(candidates)
136	        order = np.argsort(country_ids, kind="stable")
137	        segments: dict[str, tuple[int, int]] = {}
138	        position = 0
139	        for cid in range(len(country_names)):
140	            count = len(texts_by_country[cid])
141	            if count:
142	                segments[country_names[cid]] = (position, count)
143	                position += count
144	
145	        print(f"[dense] Encoding {n:,} candidate texts on device '{index.device}' "
146	              f"(model={encoder}, dim={index.dim}) ...")
147	        memmap_path = os.path.join(cache_dir, "embeddings.fp16.npy")
148	        memmap = np.lib.format.open_memmap(memmap_path, mode="w+", dtype=np.float16, shape=(n, index.dim))
149	        for cid in range(len(country_names)):
150	            country = country_names[cid]
151	            start, count = segments.get(country, (0, 0))
152	            texts = texts_by_country[cid]
153	            for chunk_start in range(0, count, ENCODE_CHUNK):
154	                chunk = texts[chunk_start:chunk_start + ENCODE_CHUNK]
155	                vectors = index._encode_texts(chunk)
156	                memmap[start + chunk_start:start + chunk_start + len(chunk)] = vectors.astype(np.float16)
157	                done = min(chunk_start + len(chunk), count)
158	                print(f"[dense]   {country or '<empty>'}: encoded {done:,}/{count:,}")
159	            texts_by_country[cid] = None  # free the text list as we go
160	        memmap.flush()
161	        del memmap
162	
163	        order_path = os.path.join(cache_dir, "order.npy")
164	        np.save(order_path, order.astype(np.int64))
165	        meta = {
166	            "encoder": encoder,
167	            "text_version": ENCODER_TEXT_VERSION,
168	            "dim": index.dim,
169	            "count": n,
170	            "segments": {country: [int(s), int(c)] for country, (s, c) in segments.items()},
171	        }
172	        with open(os.path.join(cache_dir, "dense_meta.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
173	            json.dump(meta, handle, indent=2)
174	        index.order = order.astype(np.int64)
175	        index.segments = segments
176	        index.count = n
177	        print(f"[dense] Cache written to {cache_dir}")
178	        return index
179	
180	    @classmethod
181	    def load(cls, cache_dir: str, encoder: str, device: str, encode_batch: int) -> "DenseIndex | None":
182	        meta_path = os.path.join(cache_dir, "dense_meta.json")
183	        order_path = os.path.join(cache_dir, "order.npy")
184	        memmap_path = os.path.join(cache_dir, "embeddings.fp16.npy")
185	        if not (os.path.isfile(meta_path) and os.path.isfile(order_path) and os.path.isfile(memmap_path)):
186	            return None
187	        with open(meta_path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
188	            meta = json.load(handle)
189	        index = cls(cache_dir, meta["encoder"], device, encode_batch)
190	        index.dim = int(meta["dim"])
191	        index.count = int(meta["count"])
192	        index.segments = {country: (int(start), int(count)) for country, (start, count) in meta["segments"].items()}
193	        index.order = np.load(order_path)
194	        index._load_model()
195	        print(f"[dense] Reusing cached embeddings: {index.count:,} vectors, "
196	              f"{len(index.segments)} countries, dim={index.dim}")
197	        return index
198	
199	    def _load_model(self):
200	        if not HAVE_DENSE:
201	            raise RuntimeError("sentence-transformers/torch not installed; dense retrieval unavailable")
202	        print(f"[dense] Loading encoder '{self.encoder}' on device '{self.device}' ...")
203	        self._model = SentenceTransformer(self.encoder, device=self.device)
204	        if self.device_is_cuda:
205	            try:
206	                self._model.half()
207	            except Exception:
208	                pass
209	        if hasattr(self._model, "get_embedding_dimension"):
210	            self.dim = int(self._model.get_embedding_dimension())
211	        else:  # sentence-transformers < 5
212	            self.dim = int(self._model.get_sentence_embedding_dimension())
213	
214	    # -- search -----------------------------------------------------------
215	
216	    def _encode_texts(self, texts: list[str]) -> np.ndarray:
217	        vectors = self._model.encode(
218	            texts,
219	            batch_size=self.encode_batch,
220	            show_progress_bar=False,
221	            normalize_embeddings=True,
222	            convert_to_numpy=True,
223	        )
224	        return np.asarray(vectors, dtype=np.float32)
225	
226	    def _open_memmap(self) -> np.ndarray:
227	        if self._memmap is None:
228	            self._memmap = np.load(os.path.join(self.cache_dir, "embeddings.fp16.npy"), mmap_mode="r")
229	        return self._memmap
230	
231	    def search(self, s1_batch: pd.DataFrame, top_k: int) -> dict[str, list[tuple[int, float, int]]]:
232	        """Dense top-k per S1 entity: entity_id -> [(candidate row, cosine, rank)].
233	
234	        The country segment is streamed from the fp16 memmap in SEARCH_CHUNK
235	        blocks rather than loaded whole, so peak device memory is one chunk no
236	        matter how large the segment is. Each chunk is scored against every
237	        query of the country before the next chunk is fetched; repeated passes
238	        over a segment are served from the OS page cache.
239	        """
240	        if self._model is None:
241	            return {}
242	        groups: dict[str, list[tuple[str, str]]] = defaultdict(list)
243	        for entity_id, name, address, country in s1_batch[
244	            ["entity_id", "business_name", "business_address", "country"]
245	        ].itertuples(index=False, name=None):
246	            prepared = prepare_record(name, address, country)
247	            groups[str(prepared["country"])].append((entity_id, encoder_text(prepared)))
248	
249	        results: dict[str, list[tuple[int, float, int]]] = {}
250	        source = self._open_memmap()
251	        for country, items in groups.items():
252	            segment = self.segments.get(country)
253	            if segment is None:
254	                continue
255	            start, count = segment
256	            k = min(top_k, count)
257	            if k <= 0:
258	                continue
259	            dtype = torch.float16 if self.device_is_cuda else torch.float32
260	            queries = torch.from_numpy(
261	                self._encode_texts([text for _, text in items])
262	            ).to(device=self.device, dtype=dtype)
263	            group_bounds = [
264	                (offset, min(offset + QUERY_GROUP, len(items)))
265	                for offset in range(0, len(items), QUERY_GROUP)
266	            ]
267	            best: list[tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor] | None] = [None] * len(group_bounds)
268	            for chunk_start in range(0, count, SEARCH_CHUNK):
269	                chunk_end = min(chunk_start + SEARCH_CHUNK, count)
270	                block = np.array(source[start + chunk_start:start + chunk_end])
271	                chunk = torch.from_numpy(block).to(device=self.device, dtype=dtype)
272	                for group_index, (group_start, group_end) in enumerate(group_bounds):
273	                    sims = queries[group_start:group_end] @ chunk.t()
274	                    chunk_k = min(k, chunk_end - chunk_start)
275	                    scores_chunk, positions_chunk = torch.topk(sims, chunk_k, dim=1)
276	                    positions_chunk = positions_chunk + chunk_start
277	                    current = best[group_index]
278	                    if current is None:
279	                        best[group_index] = (scores_chunk, positions_chunk)
280	                        continue
281	                    scores, positions = current
282	                    scores = torch.cat([scores, scores_chunk], dim=1)
283	                    positions = torch.cat([positions, positions_chunk], dim=1)
284	                    if scores.shape[1] > k:
285	                        scores, merge_order = torch.topk(scores, k, dim=1)
286	                        positions = torch.gather(positions, 1, merge_order)
287	                    best[group_index] = (scores, positions)
288	                del chunk
289	            del queries
290	            if self.device_is_cuda:
291	                torch.cuda.empty_cache()
292	            print(f"[dense] Searched segment {country!r}: {count:,} vectors x {len(items):,} queries")
293	            for group_index, (group_start, group_end) in enumerate(group_bounds):
294	                scores, positions = best[group_index]
295	                scores_np = scores.float().cpu().numpy()
296	                positions_np = positions.cpu().numpy()
297	                for row_index in range(group_end - group_start):
298	                    entity_id = items[group_start + row_index][0]
299	                    hits = []
300	                    for rank in range(scores_np.shape[1]):
301	                        position = int(positions_np[row_index, rank])
302	                        candidate_row = int(self.order[start + position])
303	                        hits.append((candidate_row, float(scores_np[row_index, rank]), rank + 1))
304	                    results[entity_id] = hits
305	        return results
306	
307	
308	def merge_hits(
309	    lexical_hits: list[CandidateHit],
310	    dense_hits: list[tuple[int, float, int]],
311	    top_k: int,
312	) -> list[CandidateHit]:
313	    """Reciprocal-rank fusion of the two retrieval modes."""
314	    lexical_by_row = {hit.row: hit for hit in lexical_hits}
315	    dense_by_row = {row: (score, rank) for row, score, rank in dense_hits}
316	    fused: list[tuple[float, int, CandidateHit | None, float, int]] = []
317	    for row in set(lexical_by_row) | set(dense_by_row):
318	        lexical = lexical_by_row.get(row)
319	        dense_score, dense_rank = dense_by_row.get(row, (0.0, 0))
320	        score = 0.0
321	        if lexical is not None and lexical.lexical_rank:
322	            score += 1.0 / (RRF_K + lexical.lexical_rank)
323	        if dense_rank:
324	            score += 1.0 / (RRF_K + dense_rank)
325	        fused.append((score, row, lexical, dense_score, dense_rank))
326	    fused.sort(key=lambda item: (-item[0], item[1]))
327	    return [
328	        CandidateHit(
329	            row=row,
330	            retrieval_score=float(score),
331	            lexical_score=(lexical.lexical_score if lexical is not None else 0.0),
332	            lexical_pass_count=(lexical.lexical_pass_count if lexical is not None else 0),
333	            lexical_rank=(lexical.lexical_rank if lexical is not None else 0),
334	            dense_score=float(dense_score),
335	            dense_rank=int(dense_rank),
336	        )
337	        for score, row, lexical, dense_score, dense_rank in fused[:top_k]
338	    ]
339	
340	
341	class HybridIndex:
342	    """Lexical index + optional dense index, merged per S1 entity."""
343	
344	    def __init__(self, lexical: CandidateIndex, dense: DenseIndex | None,
345	                 top_k: int, lexical_k: int, dense_k: int):
346	        self.lexical = lexical
347	        self.dense = dense
348	        self.top_k = top_k
349	        self.lexical_k = lexical_k
350	        self.dense_k = dense_k
351	
352	    @classmethod
353	    def build(
354	        cls,
355	        candidates: pd.DataFrame,
356	        data_dir: str,
357	        model_dir: str = "models",
358	        top_k: int = DEFAULT_TOP_K,
359	        lexical_k: int = DEFAULT_LEXICAL_K,
360	        dense_k: int = DEFAULT_DENSE_K,
361	        encoder: str = DEFAULT_ENCODER,
362	        device: str = "auto",
363	        encode_batch: int = DEFAULT_ENCODE_BATCH,
364	        dense_enabled: bool = True,
365	        cand_limit: int | None = None,
366	    ) -> "HybridIndex":
367	        if cand_limit is not None:
368	            candidates = candidates.head(cand_limit).copy()
369	            print(f"[hybrid] cand_limit={cand_limit}: using {len(candidates):,} candidate rows")
370	        if dense_enabled and not HAVE_DENSE:
371	            print("[hybrid] WARNING: torch/sentence-transformers unavailable - "
372	                  "falling back to lexical-only retrieval.")
373	            dense_enabled = False
374	
375	        cache_dir = None
376	        dense_index = None
377	        fingerprint = None
378	        if dense_enabled:
379	            prefix = Path(data_dir).name
380	            suffix = f"_sub{cand_limit}" if cand_limit is not None else ""
381	            cache_dir = os.path.join(model_dir, "cache", f"{prefix}_dense{suffix}")
382	            fingerprint = _cache_fingerprint(source_paths(data_dir), encoder, cand_limit)
383	            meta_path = os.path.join(cache_dir, "dense_meta.json")
384	            if os.path.isfile(meta_path):
385	                with open(meta_path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
386	                    stored = json.load(handle)
387	                if (stored.get("fingerprint") == fingerprint
388	                        and stored.get("encoder") == encoder
389	                        and stored.get("text_version") == ENCODER_TEXT_VERSION):
390	                    dense_index = DenseIndex.load(cache_dir, encoder, device, encode_batch)
391	                else:
392	                    print(f"[dense] Cache fingerprint mismatch - re-encoding into {cache_dir}")
393	
394	        n_rows = len(candidates)
395	        print(f"[hybrid] Building indexes for {n_rows:,} S2/S3 records "
396	              f"(lexical_k={lexical_k}, dense_k={dense_k}, top_k={top_k}) ...")
397	        key_arrays = [np.empty(n_rows, dtype=np.uint64) for _ in range(11)]
398	        need_dense = dense_enabled and dense_index is None
399	        country_ids = np.empty(n_rows, dtype=np.int32) if need_dense else None
400	        country_names: dict[int, str] = {}
401	        country_to_cid: dict[str, int] = {}
402	        texts_by_country: dict[int, list[str]] = defaultdict(list) if need_dense else {}
403	
404	        for row_idx, prepared in iter_prepared(candidates):
405	            for array, value in zip(key_arrays, record_key_values(prepared)):
406	                array[row_idx] = _fingerprint(value)
407	            if need_dense:
408	                country = str(prepared["country"])
409	                cid = country_to_cid.get(country)
410	                if cid is None:
411	                    cid = len(country_names)
412	                    country_to_cid[country] = cid
413	                    country_names[cid] = country
414	                country_ids[row_idx] = cid
415	                texts_by_country[cid].append(encoder_text(prepared))
416	            if (row_idx + 1) % 500_000 == 0:
417	                print(f"[hybrid]   prepared {row_idx + 1:,}/{n_rows:,} candidate rows")
418	
419	        lexical = CandidateIndex.from_key_arrays(key_arrays)
420	
421	        if need_dense:
422	            dense_index = DenseIndex.build(
423	                candidates, texts_by_country, country_ids, country_names,
424	                cache_dir, encoder, device, encode_batch,
425	            )
426	            meta_path = os.path.join(cache_dir, "dense_meta.json")
427	            with open(meta_path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
428	                meta = json.load(handle)
429	            meta["fingerprint"] = fingerprint
430	            with open(meta_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
431	                json.dump(meta, handle, indent=2)
432	        return cls(lexical, dense_index, top_k, lexical_k, dense_k)
433	
434	    def retrieve_batch(self, s1_batch: pd.DataFrame, top_k: int | None = None) -> dict[str, list[CandidateHit]]:
435	        top_k = self.top_k if top_k is None else top_k
436	        lexical = lexical_retrieve_batch(s1_batch, self.lexical, top_k=self.lexical_k)
437	        if self.dense is None:
438	            return {s1_id: hits[:top_k] for s1_id, hits in lexical.items()}
439	        dense = self.dense.search(s1_batch, self.dense_k)
440	        return {
441	            s1_id: merge_hits(lexical.get(s1_id, []), dense.get(s1_id, []), top_k)
442	            for s1_id in s1_batch["entity_id"]
443	        }
444	
445	
446	def retrieve_batch(s1_batch: pd.DataFrame, index: HybridIndex, top_k: int | None = None) -> dict[str, list[CandidateHit]]:
447	    """Drop-in replacement for the lexical retrieve_batch used by train/predict."""
448	    return index.retrieve_batch(s1_batch, top_k=top_k)
449	
450	
451	def iter_country_batches(s1: pd.DataFrame, batch_size: int = 1_000):
452	    """Yield S1 batches whose rows share one country (raw column value order).
453	
454	    Country-grouped iteration keeps each dense search() call inside a single
455	    country segment, so the memmap reads stay sequential and page-cache
456	    friendly.
457	    """
458	    if len(s1) == 0:
459	        return
460	    country_values = s1["country"].astype(str).to_numpy()
461	    order = np.argsort(country_values, kind="stable")
462	    sorted_s1 = s1.iloc[order]
463	    for start in range(0, len(sorted_s1), batch_size):
464	        yield sorted_s1.iloc[start:start + batch_size]
465	
466	
467	if __name__ == "__main__":
468	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Diagnostic: hybrid retrieval for one data directory")
469	    parser.add_argument("--data-dir", default="dataset/test")
470	    parser.add_argument("--model-dir", default="models")
471	    parser.add_argument("--top-k", type=int, default=DEFAULT_TOP_K)
472	    parser.add_argument("--lexical-k", type=int, default=DEFAULT_LEXICAL_K)
473	    parser.add_argument("--dense-k", type=int, default=DEFAULT_DENSE_K)
474	    parser.add_argument("--encoder", default=DEFAULT_ENCODER)
475	    parser.add_argument("--device", default="auto")
476	    parser.add_argument("--encode-batch", type=int, default=DEFAULT_ENCODE_BATCH)
477	    parser.add_argument("--no-dense", action="store_true")
478	    parser.add_argument("--s1-limit", type=int, default=100)
479	    args = parser.parse_args()
480	
481	    s1, s2, s3 = load_sources(args.data_dir, s1_limit=args.s1_limit)
482	    candidates = pd.concat([s2, s3], ignore_index=True)
483	    index = HybridIndex.build(
484	        candidates, args.data_dir, model_dir=args.model_dir, top_k=args.top_k,
485	        lexical_k=args.lexical_k, dense_k=args.dense_k, encoder=args.encoder,
486	        device=args.device, encode_batch=args.encode_batch, dense_enabled=not args.no_dense,
487	    )
488	    for batch in iter_country_batches(s1, batch_size=50):
489	        hits_by_s1 = retrieve_batch(batch, index)
490	        for s1_id in batch["entity_id"].head(5):
491	            hits = hits_by_s1[s1_id]
492	            dense_only = [h for h in hits if h.dense_rank and not h.lexical_rank]
493	            print(f"[hybrid] {s1_id}: {len(hits)} candidates "
494	                  f"({len(dense_only)} dense-only) best={hits[0].row if hits else None}")
495	        break

### CPU + GPU together

Technically yes, but it would probably **slow or crash this laptop**:

- Candidate preparation used one CPU core, but measured only **733 seconds (~12 minutes)**. Multiprocessing could save several minutes but duplicate pandas data and exhaust 16GB RAM.
- Dense encoding/search already uses the GPU. Splitting dense search across CPU and GPU is unattractive: the CPU requires ~9.5GB fp32 for the US segment and is much slower.
- CPU still performs lexical retrieval, preprocessing, file I/O, and feeds the GPU.

The worthwhile speed optimization is increasing GPU workload per operation, such as larger query groups—not CPU/GPU splitting. We can benchmark that after securing the current Stage D result.

### Can we realistically reach 0.988?

With the **current retrieval, no**. This follows mathematically.

At hybrid@60:

- Recall ceiling: `R = 0.8138`
- Even with impossible perfect precision (`P = 1.0`):

```text
F0.5 max = 1.25 × 1 × 0.8138 / (0.25 × 1 + 0.8138)
         ≈ 0.9563
```

Even hybrid@100 recall `0.8412` has a ceiling of approximately **0.9636**.

To score `0.988`:

- At perfect precision `1.000`, recall must be at least **0.943**
- At precision `0.995`, recall must be approximately **0.961**
- At precision `0.990`, recall must be approximately **0.980**

Therefore, 0.988 requires both extraordinary retrieval and classification. From 0.705 with 36 hours remaining, **0.988 is possible in theory but not a realistic planning target**. A strong improvement remains realistic; reaching roughly 0.90–0.96 depends on what the India misses reveal. We should still iterate aggressively, but not gamble away a working submission chasing 0.988.

### What to investigate for India

Inspect **ground-truth matches missing from hybrid@60**, then classify each miss in this order:

1. **Present in lexical/dense but dropped by RRF**
   - True match appears within lexical@100 or dense@100 but not hybrid@60.
   - This means fusion or candidate limit is the problem.

2. **Absent from both retrievers**
   - This means normalization or representation is the problem.

3. Within absent matches, bucket by:
   - Latin ↔ Devanagari transliteration.
   - Abbreviations and acronyms.
   - Legal suffix differences: Ltd, Pvt, LLP, Enterprises, Traders.
   - Token reordering or concatenation.
   - Typographical/OCR errors.
   - Personal/proprietor name versus shop name.
   - Generic names with address providing the only identity signal.
   - Missing or severely shortened names/addresses.
   - PIN code, locality, city, or state abbreviation differences.
   - Source 2 versus Source 3—check whether one is disproportionately difficult.
   - True dense rank and similarity: rank 101–500 means increasing/re-ranking retrieval may recover it; very low similarity means text representation needs changing.
   - Multiple true matches per S1: determine whether we retrieve one easy variant but miss other legitimate variants.

The most important counts are:

```text
A: dropped by hybrid top-60
B: lexical-only recoverable
C: dense-only recoverable
D: neither retriever finds it
```

Those four numbers tell us whether the next iteration should change RRF/top-K, lexical normalization, dense text construction, or add transliteration.

Run Stage D now as the safe checkpoint. We likely have time for **one major retrieval iteration and possibly one smaller threshold/model iteration** afterward.

https://huggingface.co/BAAI/bge-m3




Lexical issues in datasets for dense retrieval in India primarily stem from the country’s massive linguistic diversity, where English is heavily mixed with regional languages through transliteration, code-mixing, and colloquial variations. While dense retrieval models are designed to capture semantic meaning rather than exact keyword matches, they frequently fail when the lexical formatting of the underlying dataset diverges from the reality of how Indian users search.Here is a breakdown of the primary lexical challenges in Indian text datasets and how they undermine dense retrieval performance:1. The Transliteration Mismatch (The Multi-Spelling Problem)In India, non-English words (names of entities, regional movies, or government schemes) are routinely searched in Latin/English script. Because there is no standardized spelling system for transliterating Indic scripts to Latin, a single word can have multiple lexical forms.The Issue: A user might search for "Aadhar" card, while the official dataset stores it as "Aadhaar". Similarly, a regional film or place name like "Kantara" could be written as "Kanthara".Impact on Dense Retrieval: If the pre-training text of a dense encoder (like BERT or RoBERTa) didn’t capture these exact spelling variations linked together in context, their vector embeddings will diverge in the semantic space, leading to missed retrievals.2. Code-Mixing and "Hinglish"Indian datasets and queries are frequently code-mixed (e.g., mixing Hindi vocabulary with English grammar, known as Hinglish, or doing the same with Tamil, Telugu, or Bengali).The Issue: A dataset might contain the phrase "Gas cylinder booking kaise karein" (How to book a gas cylinder).Impact on Dense Retrieval: Standard multilingual dense retrievers (like mBERT or XLM-R) are generally trained on monolingual corpora (e.g., pure Hindi or pure English). They struggle to encode the hybrid structural syntax of code-mixed data, leading to poorly aligned representations where a code-mixed query fails to match a clean English document, or vice-versa.3. Out-of-Vocabulary (OOV) Named EntitiesIndia features thousands of unique cultural entities, local brands, localized financial terms, and regional colloquialisms that are absent from global western-centric datasets.The Issue: Terms like "Chit fund", "Panchayat", "Mandi price", or "UPI PIN" represent localized context.Impact on Dense Retrieval: Tokenizers like WordPiece or Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) break these unknown words into meaningless sub-word fragments (e.g., "pan" + "chayat"). The dense model then fails to capture the coherent semantic meaning of the entity, treating it as noise.4. Over-reliance on Exact Lexical Signals in Specific SectorsIn Indian legal (e.g., Supreme Court judgments) and medical datasets, specific, formal, or archaic terminology dictates document relevance.The Issue: Legal research in India relies heavily on specific statutes, act names, or verbatim quotes.Impact on Dense Retrieval: Dense models often experience "semantic fog" where they group documents based on general topic similarity rather than capturing the precise legal nuance required. In these scenarios, traditional lexical models like BM25 often outperform off-the-shelf dense retrievers.How to Mitigate These IssuesTo fix these lexical gaps, engineering teams building search and RAG systems in India typically employ three core strategies:StrategyActionable SolutionHybrid RetrievalCombine BM25 for exact keyword matching with dense vectors to ensure localized named entities aren't dropped.Data AugmentationArtificially expand your training datasets by using LLMs to generate phonetic variations and code-mixed equivalents of target documents.Domain-Specific TokenizersTrain specialized tokenizers or fine-tune models like BAAI/bge-m3 on Indian language corpora to prevent aggressive sub-word fragmentation.

## Why India dense retrieval is weaker

The measured gap is real:

- India: lexical `0.6179`, dense `0.6233`
- US: lexical `0.7416`, dense `0.8002`
- India hybrid still reaches `0.7169`, meaning dense finds **different matches**, but ranks many true matches poorly.

Likely causes:

1. **MiniLM understands semantics, not phonetics.**  
   Business names are proper nouns; `Aadhar/Aadhaar`, transliteration variants, and typos often have no semantic relationship for an off-the-shelf encoder.

2. **Only ~4% is Latin↔Devanagari.**  
   That cannot explain the full ~16-point India/US gap. Most failures are probably Latin-script spelling variation, abbreviations, aliases, and noisy addresses.

3. **Our normalization is Western-heavy.**  
   `preprocess.py:23-54` covers `inc`, `llc`, `road`, `suite`, etc., but few Indian patterns such as `nr/near`, `opp`, `nagar`, `distt`, `tal`, `tehsil`, `village`, `po`, `ps`.

4. **Lexical blocking has sharp cutoffs.**
   - Tokens shorter than four characters are excluded: `preprocess.py:145-150`
   - Common posting lists are capped at 150: `blocking.py:150-163`
   - Only the first address number participates in one key: `blocking.py:71-79`
   - Exact hashes cannot tolerate `aa↔a`, `ee↔i`, `oo↔u`, missing letters, etc.

Candidate density and true matches per entity are nearly equal between countries, so corpus size and match multiplicity are not the explanation.

## OOM path is now hardened

I added transactional adaptive CUDA recovery:

- Search starts with 250,000 candidate rows.
- On CUDA OOM, it clears the allocator and retries the same rows with half the chunk.
- It continues down to 15,625 rows.
- Partial results are not committed before the chunk succeeds.
- It never recreates the dangerous 9.5GB CPU segment.

Relevant code: `hybrid_blocking.py:66`, `hybrid_blocking.py:232`, `hybrid_blocking.py:292-305`.

Verification passed for:

- CPU against brute force
- CUDA against brute force
- Injected CUDA OOM **after scoring**
- Retry produced identical rows, ranks, and scores

Stage C also successfully executed the actual 256×250,000 CUDA operation over both complete country segments. Stage D’s 5,000-query batch still processes groups of 256, so it does not increase peak matrix VRAM. I reduced prediction batching from 10,000 to **5,000** for host-RAM safety: `run_pipeline.py:49`.

The test candidate count is slightly smaller than train, and the same batch-256 encoder already completed train encoding. This specific overnight OOM failure is now covered.

## What the supplied research tells us

The regional-title paper is directly useful—but its improvement did **not** come from merely selecting MiniLM:

- Pretrained MiniLM Recall@16: `51.04%`
- Fine-tuned with synthetic variations and contrastive loss: `85.38%`
- Useful transformations:
  - `a↔aa`, `i↔ee`, `u↔oo`, `s↔z`, `w↔wh`
  - missing characters
  - adjacent transposition
  - missing spaces
  - keyboard errors
- Data augmentation improved Recall@16 from `68.1%` to `81.13%`.
- Contrastive loss added another ~4 points.

Therefore, the paper supports **domain fine-tuning and phonetic augmentation**, not blindly replacing our encoder.

The legal-retrieval paper is less directly applicable because it concerns long documents. Its useful lessons are tuned lexical retrieval and score-relative result selection. For our short names, character/phonetic retrieval is more appropriate than full BM25.

## BGE-M3

BGE-M3 is MIT licensed and supports dense, sparse, and ColBERT-style retrieval, but it is not the right immediate full replacement:

- 1024-dimensional vectors versus our 384
- Roughly **21GB per candidate cache** instead of ~8GB
- Approximately 2.67× more exact-search arithmetic

Take 100–200 missed Indian true pairs and tally:

1. Latin↔Devanagari

9. S2 versus S3 failure rate
10. True-match lexical rank and dense rank
11. Retrieved in top-100 but removed by hybrid@60
12. Lost because a common posting list exceeded 150
13. Names composed mainly of tokens shorter than four characters

The four decisive totals remain:

- recovered only lexically
- recovered only densely
- recovered by either but dropped from hybrid@60
- absent from both

133	    lexical_rank: int = 0  # rank in the lexical output; 0 = not lexically retrieved
134	    dense_score: float = 0.0
135	    dense_rank: int = 0  # rank in the dense output; 0 = not densely retrieved
136	
137	
138	@dataclass
139	class SortedHashIndex:
140	    hashes: np.ndarray
141	    rows: np.ndarray
142	
143	    @classmethod
144	    def from_hashes(cls, raw_hashes: np.ndarray) -> "SortedHashIndex":
145	        order = np.argsort(raw_hashes, kind="stable")
146	        rows = order.astype(np.int32, copy=False)
147	        hashes = raw_hashes[order]
148	        return cls(hashes=hashes, rows=rows)
149	
150	    def lookup_hash(self, fingerprint: np.uint64, limit: int = MAX_BLOCK_SIZE) -> np.ndarray:
151	        left = int(np.searchsorted(self.hashes, fingerprint, side="left"))
152	        right = int(np.searchsorted(self.hashes, fingerprint, side="right"))
153	        size = right - left
154	        if size <= 0:
155	            return np.empty(0, dtype=np.int32)
156	        values = self.rows[left:right]
157	        if size <= limit:
158	            return values
159	        # A common key must not create an unbounded candidate pool. Spread the
160	        # deterministic sample across the full posting list instead of keeping
161	        # only the first rows.
162	        positions = np.linspace(0, size - 1, num=limit, dtype=np.int64)
163	        return values[positions]
164	
165	
166	@dataclass
167	class CandidateIndex:
168	    exact_name: SortedHashIndex
169	    core_name: SortedHashIndex
170	    compact_name: SortedHashIndex
171	    sorted_name: SortedHashIndex
172	    compact_address: SortedHashIndex
173	    name_anchor: SortedHashIndex
174	    name_second_anchor: SortedHashIndex
175	    name_prefix: SortedHashIndex
176	    address_anchor: SortedHashIndex
177	    numeric_address: SortedHashIndex
178	    initials: SortedHashIndex
179	
180	    @classmethod
181	    def build(cls, candidates: pd.DataFrame) -> "CandidateIndex":
182	        n_rows = len(candidates)
183	        print(f"[blocking] Building bounded retrieval indexes for {n_rows:,} S2/S3 records ...")
184	        key_arrays = [np.empty(n_rows, dtype=np.uint64) for _ in range(11)]
185	        for row_idx, prepared in iter_prepared(candidates):
186	            for array, value in zip(key_arrays, record_key_values(prepared)):
187	                array[row_idx] = _fingerprint(value)
188	            if (row_idx + 1) % INDEX_PROGRESS_EVERY == 0:
189	                print(f"[blocking]   indexed {row_idx + 1:,}/{n_rows:,} candidates")
190	        return cls.from_key_arrays(key_arrays)
191	
192	    @classmethod
193	    def from_key_arrays(cls, key_arrays: list[np.ndarray]) -> "CandidateIndex":
194	        # Consumes key_arrays as it goes so the caller does not need to keep the
195	        # unsorted and sorted index sets in memory at the same time.
196	        indexes_reversed = []
197	        while key_arrays:
198	            indexes_reversed.append(SortedHashIndex.from_hashes(key_arrays.pop()))
199	        indexes = list(reversed(indexes_reversed))
200	        print("[blocking] Candidate indexes ready.")
201	        return cls(*indexes)
202	
203	    def retrieve(self, name: str, address: str, country: str, top_k: int = DEFAULT_TOP_K) -> list[CandidateHit]:
204	        prepared = prepare_record(name, address, country)
205	        scores: dict[int, list[float]] = {}
206	        for field, value, weight in record_pass_specs(prepared):
207	            if not value:
208	                continue
209	            rows = getattr(self, field).lookup_hash(_fingerprint(value))
210	            for rank, row in enumerate(rows, start=1):
211	                item = scores.setdefault(int(row), [0.0, 0.0])
212	                item[0] += weight / np.log2(rank + 1.0)
213	                item[1] += 1.0
214	
215	        ranked = sorted(scores.items(), key=lambda item: (-item[1][0], -item[1][1], item[0]))[:top_k]
216	        return [
217	            CandidateHit(
218	                row=row,
219	                retrieval_score=float(values[0]),
220	                lexical_score=float(values[0]),
221	                lexical_pass_count=int(values[1]),
222	                lexical_rank=rank,
223	            )
224	            for rank, (row, values) in enumerate(ranked, start=1)
225	        ]
226	
227	
228	def retrieve_batch(s1_batch: pd.DataFrame, index: CandidateIndex, top_k: int = DEFAULT_TOP_K) -> dict[str, list[CandidateHit]]:
229	    result: dict[str, list[CandidateHit]] = {}
230	    for entity_id, name, address, country in s1_batch[["entity_id", "business_name", "business_address", "country"]].itertuples(index=False, name=None):
231	        result[entity_id] = index.retrieve(name, address, country, top_k=top_k)
232	    return result
233	
234	
235	def candidate_ids(hits: list[CandidateHit], candidate_entity_ids: np.ndarray) -> list[str]:
236	    return [str(candidate_entity_ids[hit.row]) for hit in hits]
237	
238	
239	def run_blocking(data_dir: str, output_path: str, top_k: int = DEFAULT_TOP_K, s1_limit: int | None = None) -> None:
240	    s1, s2, s3 = load_sources(data_dir, s1_limit=s1_limit)
241	    candidates = pd.concat([s2, s3], ignore_index=True)
242	    entity_ids = candidates["entity_id"].to_numpy(copy=False)
243	    index = CandidateIndex.build(candidates)
244	    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(output_path)), exist_ok=True)
245	    with open(output_path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
246	        handle.write("source1_entity_id\tcandidate_entity_ids\n")
247	        for start in range(0, len(s1), 2_000):
248	            batch = s1.iloc[start:start + 2_000]
249	            hits_by_s1 = retrieve_batch(batch, index, top_k=top_k)
250	            for s1_id in batch["entity_id"]:
251	                ids = candidate_ids(hits_by_s1[s1_id], entity_ids)
252	                handle.write(f"{s1_id}\t{','.join(ids)}\n")
253	            print(f"[blocking] Retrieved candidates for {min(start + len(batch), len(s1)):,}/{len(s1):,} S1 rows")
254	
255	
256	if __name__ == "__main__":
257	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Generate ranked entity-resolution candidates")
258	    parser.add_argument("--data-dir", default="dataset/test")
259	    parser.add_argument("--output", default="output/candidate_pairs.tsv")
260	    parser.add_argument("--top-k", type=int, default=DEFAULT_TOP_K)
261	    parser.add_argument("--s1-limit", type=int, default=None)
262	    args = parser.parse_args()
263	    run_blocking(args.data_dir, args.output, args.top_k, args.s1_limit)

The evidence already points to a concrete distinction: the streaming paper’s gains came from **task-specific contrastive fine-tuning and millions of synthetic spelling/transliteration pairs**, not from swapping in an off-the-shelf dense model. I’m now hardening the CUDA path so an incidental VRAM spike shrinks the search chunk instead of killing Stage D.

#### Tool: Read

**Input:**

```json
{
  "file_path": "C:\\Users\\vishe\\.qoder\\tmp\\unit_check_chunked_search.py"
}
```

**Response:**

1	"""Unit check for the chunked-streaming DenseIndex.search rewrite.
2	
3	Builds a tiny synthetic fp16 cache whose top-k structure is tie-free by
4	construction: each query's anchors are standard basis vectors with
5	well-separated weights, and all filler vectors are exactly orthogonal to
6	every query (disjoint support). Compares search() output against a
7	brute-force reference on the CPU path and, when available, the CUDA path,
8	with SEARCH_CHUNK/QUERY_GROUP shrunk to force many chunks, partial query
9	groups, and a final chunk smaller than top_k.
10	"""
11	import gc
12	import sys
13	import tempfile
14	from pathlib import Path
15	
16	import numpy as np
17	import pandas as pd
18	import torch
19	
20	SRC = Path(r"C:\Vishesh\Docs\Repos\amazon_ML_challenge\code\business_entity_resolution\src")
21	sys.path.insert(0, str(SRC))
22	
23	import hybrid_blocking as hb
24	from preprocess import prepare_record
25	
26	DIM = 64  # >= 7 * max queries per country, so every query gets a disjoint anchor support
27	ANCHOR_WEIGHTS = [0.90, 0.70, 0.52, 0.36, 0.22, 0.12, 0.05]
28	TOP_K = 5
29	rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
30	
31	
32	def unit_rows(v):
33	    v = np.asarray(v, dtype=np.float64)
34	    return (v / np.linalg.norm(v, axis=1, keepdims=True)).astype(np.float32)
35	
36	
37	# (raw country, segment size, queries) — 'de' makes the final chunk (141 % 137 = 4 rows) smaller than top_k
38	raw_specs = [("in", 700, 5), ("us", 500, 4), ("zz", 3, 1), ("de", 141, 1)]
39	
40	segments: dict[str, tuple[int, int]] = {}
41	emb_blocks = []
42	queries_by_key: dict[str, list[tuple[str, np.ndarray]]] = {}
43	position = 0
44	for raw, n, nq in raw_specs:
45	    key = str(prepare_record("x", "y", raw)["country"])
46	    assert key not in segments, f"country normalization collision on {raw!r} -> {key!r}"
47	    n_anchors = min(n, 7 * nq)
48	    block = np.zeros((n, DIM), dtype=np.float32)
49	    for j in range(nq):
50	        for i in range(7 if n >= 7 * nq else min(7, n - 7 * j)):
51	            block[7 * j + i, 7 * j + i] = 1.0  # query j's anchor i: basis vector e_{7j+i}
52	    filler = rng.normal(size=(n - n_anchors, DIM))
53	    filler[:, :7 * nq] = 0.0  # orthogonal to every query of this country
54	    block[n_anchors:] = unit_rows(filler)
55	    for j in range(nq):
56	        weights = [ANCHOR_WEIGHTS[(i + 2 * j) % 7] for i in range(7)]
57	        q = np.zeros(DIM, dtype=np.float64)
58	        q[7 * j:7 * j + 7] = weights
59	        q = unit_rows(q.reshape(1, -1))[0]
60	        queries_by_key.setdefault(key, []).append((f"S1_{raw}_{j}", q))
61	    emb_blocks.append(block.astype(np.float16))
62	    segments[key] = (position, n)
63	    position += n
64	
65	total = position
66	emb = np.concatenate(emb_blocks)
67	order = rng.permutation(total).astype(np.int64)  # memmap position -> candidate row
68	
69	# S1 rows (plus one entity from an unknown country, which must be skipped)
70	q_by_text: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
71	s1_rows = []
72	for raw, _n, _nq in raw_specs:
73	    for eid, _q in queries_by_key[str(prepare_record("x", "y", raw)["country"])]:
74	        j = int(eid.rsplit("_", 1)[1])
75	        name, addr, country = f"query {raw} {j}", f"street {raw} {j}", raw
76	        s1_rows.append((eid, name, addr, country))
77	        text = hb.encoder_text(prepare_record(name, addr, country))
78	        assert text not in q_by_text
79	        q_by_text[text] = _q
80	unknown_key = str(prepare_record("x", "y", "xx")["country"])
81	assert unknown_key not in segments, f"unknown country {unknown_key!r} unexpectedly collides"
82	s1_rows.append(("S1_xx_0", "query xx 0", "street xx 0", "xx"))
83	s1_batch = pd.DataFrame(
84	    s1_rows, columns=["entity_id", "business_name", "business_address", "country"]
85	)
86	
87	# Brute-force reference in float32 from the fp16-stored embeddings
88	E32 = emb.astype(np.float32)
89	reference: dict[str, list[tuple[int, float]]] = {}
90	for eid, name, addr, country in s1_rows:
91	    if eid == "S1_xx_0":
92	        continue
93	    key = str(prepare_record(name, addr, country)["country"])
94	    start, count = segments[key]
95	    q = q_by_text[hb.encoder_text(prepare_record(name, addr, country))]
96	    sims = E32[start:start + count] @ q
97	    k = min(TOP_K, count)
98	    top = np.argsort(-sims, kind="stable")[:k]
99	    reference[eid] = [(int(order[start + int(p)]), float(sims[p])) for p in top]
100	
101	
102	def build_index(cache_dir: str, device: str) -> hb.DenseIndex:
103	    index = object.__new__(hb.DenseIndex)
104	    index.cache_dir = cache_dir
105	    index.encoder = "stub-encoder"
106	    index.encode_batch = 8
107	    index.device = device
108	    index.device_is_cuda = device.startswith("cuda")
109	    index.dim = DIM
110	    index.count = total
111	    index.segments = segments
112	    index.order = order
113	    index._memmap = None
114	    index._model = object()
115	    index._encode_texts = lambda texts: np.stack([q_by_text[t] for t in texts])
116	    return index
117	
118	
119	def run_case(device: str, score_tol: float) -> None:
120	    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
121	        np.save(Path(tmp) / "embeddings.fp16.npy", emb)
122	        np.save(Path(tmp) / "order.npy", order)
123	        index = build_index(tmp, device)
124	        results = index.search(s1_batch, TOP_K)
125	        index._memmap = None  # release the Windows file mapping before cleanup

## Why India dense retrieval is weaker

The measured gap is real:

- India: lexical `0.6179`, dense `0.6233`
- US: lexical `0.7416`, dense `0.8002`
- India hybrid still reaches `0.7169`, meaning dense finds **different matches**, but ranks many true matches poorly.

Likely causes:

1. **MiniLM understands semantics, not phonetics.**  
   Business names are proper nouns; `Aadhar/Aadhaar`, transliteration variants, and typos often have no semantic relationship for an off-the-shelf encoder.

2. **Only ~4% is Latin↔Devanagari.**  
   That cannot explain the full ~16-point India/US gap. Most failures are probably Latin-script spelling variation, abbreviations, aliases, and noisy addresses.

3. **Our normalization is Western-heavy.**  
   `preprocess.py:23-54` covers `inc`, `llc`, `road`, `suite`, etc., but few Indian patterns such as `nr/near`, `opp`, `nagar`, `distt`, `tal`, `tehsil`, `village`, `po`, `ps`.

4. **Lexical blocking has sharp cutoffs.**
   - Tokens shorter than four characters are excluded: `preprocess.py:145-150`
   - Common posting lists are capped at 150: `blocking.py:150-163`
   - Only the first address number participates in one key: `blocking.py:71-79`
   - Exact hashes cannot tolerate `aa↔a`, `ee↔i`, `oo↔u`, missing letters, etc.

Candidate density and true matches per entity are nearly equal between countries, so corpus size and match multiplicity are not the explanation.

## OOM path is now hardened

I added transactional adaptive CUDA recovery:

- Search starts with 250,000 candidate rows.
- On CUDA OOM, it clears the allocator and retries the same rows with half the chunk.
- It continues down to 15,625 rows.
- Partial results are not committed before the chunk succeeds.
- It never recreates the dangerous 9.5GB CPU segment.

Relevant code: `hybrid_blocking.py:66`, `hybrid_blocking.py:232`, `hybrid_blocking.py:292-305`.

Verification passed for:

- CPU against brute force
- CUDA against brute force
- Injected CUDA OOM **after scoring**
- Retry produced identical rows, ranks, and scores

Stage C also successfully executed the actual 256×250,000 CUDA operation over both complete country segments. Stage D’s 5,000-query batch still processes groups of 256, so it does not increase peak matrix VRAM. I reduced prediction batching from 10,000 to **5,000** for host-RAM safety: `run_pipeline.py:49`.

The test candidate count is slightly smaller than train, and the same batch-256 encoder already completed train encoding. This specific overnight OOM failure is now covered.

## What the supplied research tells us

The regional-title paper is directly useful—but its improvement did **not** come from merely selecting MiniLM:

- Pretrained MiniLM Recall@16: `51.04%`
- Fine-tuned with synthetic variations and contrastive loss: `85.38%`
- Useful transformations:
  - `a↔aa`, `i↔ee`, `u↔oo`, `s↔z`, `w↔wh`
  - missing characters
  - adjacent transposition
  - missing spaces
  - keyboard errors
- Data augmentation improved Recall@16 from `68.1%` to `81.13%`.
- Contrastive loss added another ~4 points.

Therefore, the paper supports **domain fine-tuning and phonetic augmentation**, not blindly replacing our encoder.

The legal-retrieval paper is less directly applicable because it concerns long documents. Its useful lessons are tuned lexical retrieval and score-relative result selection. For our short names, character/phonetic retrieval is more appropriate than full BM25.

## BGE-M3

BGE-M3 is MIT licensed and supports dense, sparse, and ColBERT-style retrieval, but it is not the right immediate full replacement:

- 1024-dimensional vectors versus our 384
- Roughly **21GB per candidate cache** instead of ~8GB
- Approximately 2.67× more exact-search arithmetic
- XLM-R-large backbone, much slower than MiniLM on the RTX 3050
- No demonstrated business-entity/transliteration result on its model card

It could consume most of the remaining 36 hours without guaranteeing improvement. A small pairwise experiment on India misses is reasonable later; full re-encoding is not yet justified.

## What you should inspect manually

Take 100–200 missed Indian true pairs and tally:

1. Latin↔Devanagari
2. Latin↔Latin phonetic variation
3. Missing/extra letters or spaces
4. Abbreviations and legal suffixes
5. Proprietor name versus shop name
6. Generic business name where address is decisive
7. Indian address abbreviations/formats
8. PIN/locality/house-number agreement
9. S2 versus S3 failure rate
10. True-match lexical rank and dense rank
11. Retrieved in top-100 but removed by hybrid@60
12. Lost because a common posting list exceeded 150
13. Names composed mainly of tokens shorter than four characters

The four decisive totals remain:

- recovered only lexically
- recovered only densely
- recovered by either but dropped from hybrid@60
- absent from both

## Realistic 0.988 outlook

We should pursue it, but current retrieval mathematically cannot produce it. At `R=0.8138`, even perfect precision caps F0.5 around `0.956`.

Our best 36-hour route is:

1. Run Stage D and secure a valid submission.
2. Diagnose India misses.
3. Add evidence-backed phonetic/transliteration lexical keys.
4. Re-measure recall before retraining.
5. If insufficient, fine-tune MiniLM using real matched pairs plus synthetic variations and hard negatives.
6. Tune precision thresholds after retrieval improves.

You can now safely launch:


148	        return cls(hashes=hashes, rows=rows)
149	
150	    def lookup_hash(self, fingerprint: np.uint64, limit: int = MAX_BLOCK_SIZE) -> np.ndarray:
151	        left = int(np.searchsorted(self.hashes, fingerprint, side="left"))
152	        right = int(np.searchsorted(self.hashes, fingerprint, side="right"))
153	        size = right - left
154	        if size <= 0:
155	            return np.empty(0, dtype=np.int32)
156	        values = self.rows[left:right]
157	        if size <= limit:
158	            return values
159	        # A common key must not create an unbounded candidate pool. Spread the
160	        # deterministic sample across the full posting list instead of keeping
161	        # only the first rows.
162	        positions = np.linspace(0, size - 1, num=limit, dtype=np.int64)
163	        return values[positions]
164	
165	
166	@dataclass
167	class CandidateIndex:
168	    exact_name: SortedHashIndex
169	    core_name: SortedHashIndex
170	    compact_name: SortedHashIndex
171	    sorted_name: SortedHashIndex
172	    compact_address: SortedHashIndex
173	    name_anchor: SortedHashIndex
174	    name_second_anchor: SortedHashIndex
175	    name_prefix: SortedHashIndex
176	    address_anchor: SortedHashIndex
177	    numeric_address: SortedHashIndex
178	    initials: SortedHashIndex
179	
180	    @classmethod
181	    def build(cls, candidates: pd.DataFrame) -> "CandidateIndex":
182	        n_rows = len(candidates)
183	        print(f"[blocking] Building bounded retrieval indexes for {n_rows:,} S2/S3 records ...")
184	        key_arrays = [np.empty(n_rows, dtype=np.uint64) for _ in range(11)]
185	        for row_idx, prepared in iter_prepared(candidates):
186	            for array, value in zip(key_arrays, record_key_values(prepared)):
187	                array[row_idx] = _fingerprint(value)
188	            if (row_idx + 1) % INDEX_PROGRESS_EVERY == 0:
189	                print(f"[blocking]   indexed {row_idx + 1:,}/{n_rows:,} candidates")
190	        return cls.from_key_arrays(key_arrays)
191	
192	    @classmethod
193	    def from_key_arrays(cls, key_arrays: list[np.ndarray]) -> "CandidateIndex":
194	        # Consumes key_arrays as it goes so the caller does not need to keep the
195	        # unsorted and sorted index sets in memory at the same time.
196	        indexes_reversed = []
197	        while key_arrays:
198	            indexes_reversed.append(SortedHashIndex.from_hashes(key_arrays.pop()))
199	        indexes = list(reversed(indexes_reversed))
200	        print("[blocking] Candidate indexes ready.")
201	        return cls(*indexes)
202	
203	    def retrieve(self, name: str, address: str, country: str, top_k: int = DEFAULT_TOP_K) -> list[CandidateHit]:
204	        prepared = prepare_record(name, address, country)
205	        scores: dict[int, list[float]] = {}
206	        for field, value, weight in record_pass_specs(prepared):
207	            if not value:
208	                continue
209	            rows = getattr(self, field).lookup_hash(_fingerprint(value))
210	            for rank, row in enumerate(rows, start=1):
211	                item = scores.setdefault(int(row), [0.0, 0.0])
212	                item[0] += weight / np.log2(rank + 1.0)
213	                item[1] += 1.0
214	
215	        ranked = sorted(scores.items(), key=lambda item: (-item[1][0], -item[1][1], item[0]))[:top_k]
216	        return [
217	            CandidateHit(
218	                row=row,
219	                retrieval_score=float(values[0]),
220	                lexical_score=float(values[0]),
221	                lexical_pass_count=int(values[1]),
222	                lexical_rank=rank,
223	            )
224	            for rank, (row, values) in enumerate(ranked, start=1)
225	        ]
226	
227	
228	def retrieve_batch(s1_batch: pd.DataFrame, index: CandidateIndex, top_k: int = DEFAULT_TOP_K) -> dict[str, list[CandidateHit]]:
229	    result: dict[str, list[CandidateHit]] = {}
230	    for entity_id, name, address, country in s1_batch[["entity_id", "business_name", "business_address", "country"]].itertuples(index=False, name=None):
231	        result[entity_id] = index.retrieve(name, address, country, top_k=top_k)
232	    return result
233	
234	
235	def candidate_ids(hits: list[CandidateHit], candidate_entity_ids: np.ndarray) -> list[str]:
236	    return [str(candidate_entity_ids[hit.row]) for hit in hits]
237	
238	
239	def run_blocking(data_dir: str, output_path: str, top_k: int = DEFAULT_TOP_K, s1_limit: int | None = None) -> None:
240	    s1, s2, s3 = load_sources(data_dir, s1_limit=s1_limit)
241	    candidates = pd.concat([s2, s3], ignore_index=True)
242	    entity_ids = candidates["entity_id"].to_numpy(copy=False)
243	    index = CandidateIndex.build(candidates)
244	    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(output_path)), exist_ok=True)
245	    with open(output_path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
246	        handle.write("source1_entity_id\tcandidate_entity_ids\n")
247	        for start in range(0, len(s1), 2_000):
248	            batch = s1.iloc[start:start + 2_000]
249	            hits_by_s1 = retrieve_batch(batch, index, top_k=top_k)
250	            for s1_id in batch["entity_id"]:
251	                ids = candidate_ids(hits_by_s1[s1_id], entity_ids)
252	                handle.write(f"{s1_id}\t{','.join(ids)}\n")
253	            print(f"[blocking] Retrieved candidates for {min(start + len(batch), len(s1)):,}/{len(s1):,} S1 rows")
254	
255	
256	if __name__ == "__main__":
257	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Generate ranked entity-resolution candidates")
258	    parser.add_argument("--data-dir", default="dataset/test")
259	    parser.add_argument("--output", default="output/candidate_pairs.tsv")
260	    parser.add_argument("--top-k", type=int, default=DEFAULT_TOP_K)
261	    parser.add_argument("--s1-limit", type=int, default=None)
262	    args = parser.parse_args()
263	    run_blocking(args.data_dir, args.output, args.top_k, args.s1_limit)
